The fifteenth series of the [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_television "British television") [science fiction television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_fiction_on_television "Science fiction on television") programme _[Doctor Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who "Doctor Who")_ premiered on 12 April 2025. This series is also known as "Season Two" following the production changes and the acquisition of _Doctor Who_'s international broadcasting rights by [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney%2B "Disney+") prior to the previous series. It is the sixth series led by [Russell T Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell_T_Davies "Russell T Davies") as head writer and executive producer and the second since his return to the show in 2023, having previously worked on it from 2005 to 2010. This series is the fifteenth to air following the programme's revival in 2005, and is the forty-first season overall.

This is the second and final series to star [Ncuti Gatwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa "Ncuti Gatwa") as the [Fifteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor "Fifteenth Doctor"), an incarnation of [the Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Doctor "The Doctor"), an alien [Time Lord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Lord "Time Lord") who travels through time and space in the [TARDIS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TARDIS "TARDIS"), which appears to be a British [police box](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_box "Police box") from the outside. [Varada Sethu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu "Varada Sethu") joins the series as new [companion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Companion_/(Doctor_Who/) "Companion (Doctor Who)") [Belinda Chandra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra "Belinda Chandra"), with [Millie Gibson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millie_Gibson "Millie Gibson") also featuring as [Ruby Sunday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruby_Sunday "Ruby Sunday"), the previous series' companion, for her second and final series in the role. The series was preceded by a [Christmas episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joy_to_the_World_/(Doctor_Who/) "Joy to the World (Doctor Who)") in December 2024, written by former showrunner and head writer [Steven Moffat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Moffat "Steven Moffat"), where [Nicola Coughlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicola_Coughlan "Nicola Coughlan") appears as a one-off companion.

The series consists of eight episodes, directed by Alex Sanjiv Pillai, [Peter Hoar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hoar "Peter Hoar"), [Amanda Brotchie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanda_Brotchie "Amanda Brotchie"), Ben A. Williams, and Makalla McPherson. Alongside Davies, who wrote four episodes and co-wrote a further one, the writers include [Juno Dawson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juno_Dawson "Juno Dawson"), [Inua Ellams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams "Inua Ellams"), [Pete McTighe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_McTighe "Pete McTighe"), and Sharma Angel-Walfall. Filming began in October 2023 and concluded in May 2024.

Notes

1.  **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_ref-4)** The first seven episodes for the fifteenth series were released simultaneously at 8 a.m. [BST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Summer_Time "British Summer Time") in the United Kingdom on [BBC iPlayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_iPlayer "BBC iPlayer") (followed by a 7 p.m. BBC One broadcast the same day), and at 12 a.m. [PT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time "Pacific Time") in the United States on [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney%2B "Disney+").[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-VarietyApril-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-DWFuton-2) The final episode was released simultaneously at 7 p.m. BST in the United Kingdom on BBC iPlayer and BBC One, and at 11 a.m. PT in the United States on Disney+.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-DWFuton-2)[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-RealityWarReleaseTime-3)
2.  **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_ref-7)** As seen in "[Midnight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight_/(Doctor_Who/) "Midnight (Doctor Who)")" (2008)

[Ncuti Gatwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa "Ncuti Gatwa") confirmed that he would return for a second series in July 2023.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-8) In November 2023, it was announced that [Nicola Coughlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicola_Coughlan "Nicola Coughlan") would appear as the companion in the 2024 Christmas special.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-9)[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-JoytotheWorld-10) [Millie Gibson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millie_Gibson "Millie Gibson") was revealed to be filming for her second series in November 2023,[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-Gibson-11) though reports emerged in January 2024 that Gibson would be leaving the show after the fourteenth series, to be replaced by [Varada Sethu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu "Varada Sethu").[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-12) However, in April 2024 it was announced that Gibson and Sethu would appear concurrently throughout the series.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-13)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-14) Subsequent promotional material foregrounded Gatwa and Sethu as the series' "TARDIS team", highlighting them as the first to consist solely of people of colour, with Gibson described as an "outgoing series regular".[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-15) Gibson appeared in the fourth episode, "[Lucky Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucky_Day_/(Doctor_Who/) "Lucky Day (Doctor Who)")", and appears in the seventh and eighth episodes, "[Wish World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wish_World "Wish World")" / "[The Reality War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War "The Reality War")".[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-16) Sethu made a surprise appearance in the series prior in "[Boom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boom_/(Doctor_Who/) "Boom (Doctor Who)")" (2024) as Mundy Flynn before her debut as the new companion. On 27 July, it was announced at [San Diego Comic-Con](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Comic-Con "San Diego Comic-Con") that Sethu's character would be called Belinda Chandra.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-17) It is later revealed in "[The Robot Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Robot_Revolution "The Robot Revolution")" that Mundy is a descendant of Belinda.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-18)

[Alan Cumming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Cumming "Alan Cumming") guest starred in "[Lux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lux_/(Doctor_Who/) "Lux (Doctor Who)")" as a cartoon character named "Mr Ring-a-Ding"; he had previously appeared in the show as King [James VI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_VI "James VI") in "[The Witchfinders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Witchfinders "The Witchfinders")" (2018). Davies stated that only Cumming could give the character "so much wit, malice, danger and fun".[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-VarietyApril-1) [Rose Ayling-Ellis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_Ayling-Ellis "Rose Ayling-Ellis")[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-19) and [Christopher Chung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Chung_/(actor/) "Christopher Chung (actor)") appears in "[The Well](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Well_/(Doctor_Who/) "The Well (Doctor Who)")" as characters Aliss and Cassio, respectively.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-20)[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-21) [Jonah Hauer-King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonah_Hauer-King "Jonah Hauer-King") portrayed Conrad in "[Lucky Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucky_Day_/(Doctor_Who/) "Lucky Day (Doctor Who)")", a [podcaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Podcaster "Podcaster") and Ruby's boyfriend.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-Gibson-11)[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-22) [Jemma Redgrave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jemma_Redgrave "Jemma Redgrave") also returned as [Kate Lethbridge-Stewart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Lethbridge-Stewart "Kate Lethbridge-Stewart") in the same episode.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-23) Following the episode's broadcast, Gibson revealed in an interview that Hauer-King would also appear later on in the series.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-24) [Jo Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin "Jo Martin") reprises her role as the [Fugitive Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor "Fugitive Doctor") in "[The Story & the Engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Story_%26_the_Engine "The Story & the Engine")".[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-25) Showrunner [Russell T Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell_T_Davies "Russell T Davies") stated that because the episode explored the Doctor's ethnicity it "felt like Jo Martin was missing" and that he wanted to "acknowledge her" and show "she still exists". On 2 March, following the release of the series trailer, [Rylan Clark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rylan_Clark "Rylan Clark") was announced to be in the series, presenting an intergalactic song competition in "[The Interstellar Song Contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Interstellar_Song_Contest "The Interstellar Song Contest")",[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-TrailerCasting-26) an episode inspired by the [Eurovision Song Contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest "Eurovision Song Contest") which also stars [Graham Norton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graham_Norton "Graham Norton").[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-27) In the same episode, [Freddie Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Fox_/(actor/) "Freddie Fox (actor)") appears as a villain,[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-28) as well as [Kadiff Kirwan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kadiff_Kirwan "Kadiff Kirwan")[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-29) and [Charlie Condou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Condou "Charlie Condou"),[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-30) and [Carole Ann Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carole_Ann_Ford "Carole Ann Ford") reprised her role as [Susan Foreman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Foreman "Susan Foreman"), last appearing in the programme over 30 years prior in _[Dimensions in Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimensions_in_Time "Dimensions in Time")_.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-31) [Anita Dobson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anita_Dobson "Anita Dobson") appears in every episode of the series as the enigmatic Mrs Flood;[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-TrailerCasting-26) in the sixth episode, her true identity is revealed to be [The Rani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rani "The Rani"), a villainous [Time Lord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Lord "Time Lord"). [Archie Panjabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Panjabi "Archie Panjabi") was introduced as another incarnation of the Rani through a [bi-generation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bi-generation "Bi-generation") process.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-32)[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-33) [Bonnie Langford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonnie_Langford "Bonnie Langford") returns as [Mel Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mel_Bush "Mel Bush") in "[Wish World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wish_World "Wish World")", as well as [Jonathan Groff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Groff "Jonathan Groff") as Rogue in a cameo recorded in 2023 during the production of the series 14 episode, "[Rogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogue_/(Doctor_Who/) "Rogue (Doctor Who)")".[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-TrailerCasting-26)[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-34) [Jodie Whittaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Whittaker "Jodie Whittaker") reprised her role as the [Thirteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteenth_Doctor "Thirteenth Doctor") in a surprise cameo in "The Reality War".[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-35)

[Billie Piper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Piper "Billie Piper") also returned to _Doctor Who_ after previously portraying the Doctor's companion [Rose Tyler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_Tyler "Rose Tyler") last appearing in the 2013 fiftieth anniversary special, "[The Day of the Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Day_of_the_Doctor "The Day of the Doctor")",[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-36) when the Fifteenth Doctor regenerates into a character portrayed by her at the end of the episode.[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-37) While Piper's official role remains undisclosed, with the closing credits merely reading "Introducing Billie Piper",[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-38) some sources assumed her to be taking on the Doctor's sixteenth incarnation.[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-39)[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-40)[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-finalncuti-41)

Similar to the [fourteenth series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_/(series_14/) "Doctor Who (series 14)"), the fifteenth series consists of a Christmas special followed by eight regular episodes, consisting of six standalone episodes and a two-part finale.[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavies2024c6-42) The synopsis of the series was officially stated to be about an "epic quest" getting Belinda back to Earth, as the TARDIS team face "wider terrors than ever before".[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-VarietyApril-1)

Davies was writing the 2024 Christmas special by December 2022,[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavies20227-43) and the fifteenth series by June 2023.[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-44) By 18 September 2023, five of the nine scripts had been completed according to Davies's column in _[Doctor Who Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_Magazine "Doctor Who Magazine")_.[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavies202311-45) By 2 January 2024, Davies's column stated that the fifth episode was now on Draft 5, while Episode 6 was about to enter Draft 9, "getting this script ready has been epic...but all worth it, what a story!"[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavies2024b8-46)

In May 2024, former showrunner and head writer [Steven Moffat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Moffat "Steven Moffat") confirmed that he had written the 2024 Christmas special, and that it was entitled "[Joy to the World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joy_to_the_World_/(Doctor_Who/) "Joy to the World (Doctor Who)")".[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-JoytotheWorld-10) The episodes of the series itself were written by Davies and four other writers,[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavies2024a10-47) revealed on 27 January 2025 to be [Juno Dawson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juno_Dawson "Juno Dawson"), [Inua Ellams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams "Inua Ellams"), [Pete McTighe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_McTighe "Pete McTighe"), and Sharma Angel-Walfall.[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-48)

With filming for the [previous series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_14 "Doctor Who series 14") concluding in July 2023, crew were given a four-week turnaround before [pre-production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pre-production "Pre-production") started for the next series, on 14 August.[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHandcock202312-49) Each production block was given ten weeks of preparation.[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHandcock2024b10-50) The first [readthrough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Read-through "Read-through") was held on 17 October 2023.[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHandcock2024a12-51)

[Principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") began on 23 October 2023 at Bad Wolf Studios, with the 2024 Christmas special "Joy to the World" assigned to the first block, directed by Alex Sanjiv Pillai.[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuinn20234-52)[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHandcock2024a12-51)

The second block – containing the [first](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Robot_Revolution "The Robot Revolution") and [fourth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucky_Day_/(Doctor_Who/) "Lucky Day (Doctor Who)") episodes – had its first readthrough on 7 November 2023,[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-Episode_BTS-53)[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHandcock2024b10-50) and began filming on 14 November 2023, directed by [Peter Hoar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Hoar "Peter Hoar").[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHandcock2024b10-50)[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuinn20234-52) Hoar had previously directed the [sixth series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_6 "Doctor Who series 6") episode "[A Good Man Goes to War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Good_Man_Goes_to_War "A Good Man Goes to War")" (2011), and had worked with Davies on _[It's a Sin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It%27s_A_Sin_/(TV_series/) "It's A Sin (TV series)")_ and _[Nolly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nolly_/(TV_series/) "Nolly (TV series)")_.

Filming for the third block – containing the [second](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lux_/(Doctor_Who/) "Lux (Doctor Who)") and [third](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Well_/(Doctor_Who/) "The Well (Doctor Who)") episodes – began on Monday 8 January 2024 after the Christmas break,[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuinn2024a6-54) directed by [Amanda Brotchie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanda_Brotchie "Amanda Brotchie").[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavies2024b8-46)[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuinn2024b4-55) Location filming at [Penarth Pier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penarth_Pier "Penarth Pier") marked the first time that Sethu was photographed on-set as the new companion.[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-56)

Makalla McPherson and Ben A. Williams directed further blocks, with McPherson directing the [fifth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Story_%26_the_Engine "The Story & the Engine") episode, where she described she had "created a unique crane shot as the Doctor runs through a maze as they escape their captors" [\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuinn2024b4-55) and Williams directing the sixth episode, which he described as a "very big episode", and Davies described as "epic".[\[55\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-Williams-57)[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavies2024b8-46)[\[56\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuinn2024c6-58)[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavies2024c6-42) The episode from Williams is themed after the [Eurovision Song Contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest "Eurovision Song Contest").[\[57\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-insta-59)[\[58\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-60) Production for the series wrapped on 24 May 2024.[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-61)

On 21 February 2025, a trailer stating that the series would launch on 12 April was shown during the BBC's coverage of a [Six Nations Under 20s Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Six_Nations_Under_20s_Championship "2025 Six Nations Under 20s Championship") rugby match between England and Scotland.[\[65\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-12April-67) The series is released in the [UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK "UK") on [BBC iPlayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_iPlayer "BBC iPlayer") and internationally on [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney%2B "Disney+").[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavies202311-45)[\[66\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-Disney-68)

The episodes are released weekly on Saturdays at 8 a.m. [BST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Summer_Time "British Summer Time").[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-VarietyApril-1) Episodes also air on the evening of their release on [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_One "BBC One").[\[67\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-69) The sixth episode of the series, "[The Interstellar Song Contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Interstellar_Song_Contest "The Interstellar Song Contest")", was scheduled to be broadcast on BBC One on 17 May, ahead of the final of the [Eurovision Song Contest 2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest_2025 "Eurovision Song Contest 2025"). However, if the [FA Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_FA_Cup_final "2025 FA Cup final"), which was also scheduled to be played that afternoon, went to [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extra_time "Extra time"), the episode would not be shown on BBC One.[\[68\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-70) The two-part finale, "Wish World" / "The Reality War", were screened together in UK cinemas on 31 May. Release of "The Reality War" across streaming and cinemas and internationally aligned with its simultaneous evening BBC One broadcast. The episode was released at 6:50 p.m. BST in the United Kingdom, and at 11 a.m. PT in the United States.[\[69\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-71)[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-RealityWarReleaseTime-3)

Due to the terms of a deal between [BBC Worldwide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Worldwide "BBC Worldwide") and [SMG Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Media_Group "Shanghai Media Group") in [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") in May 2017, the company has first [right of refusal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_of_first_refusal "Right of first refusal") on the purchase for the Chinese market of future series of the programme until and including series 15.[\[70\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-72)[\[71\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-73)

The series is accompanied by _[Doctor Who: Unleashed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who:_Unleashed "Doctor Who: Unleashed")_, a behind-the-scenes companion show. Adopting a similar format to the former behind-the-scenes programme _[Doctor Who Confidential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_Confidential "Doctor Who Confidential")_, _Unleashed_ follows every new episode of _Doctor Who_ with a 30-minute instalment on [BBC Three](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Three "BBC Three"), hosted by [Steffan Powell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steffan_Powell "Steffan Powell").[\[72\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-74)[\[73\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-75)[\[74\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15#cite_note-UnleashedS2-76)

Director

Makalla McPherson

Episodes Broadcast: 2025

Biography

London-born Makalla McPherson started directing music videos around
2010, while also working in commercials. She made a short film called
Tight Rope in 2011, followed the next year by Tiny Steps.
Eager to become involved with television drama, McPherson won the
opportunity to direct several episodes of Doctors starting in
2013. She also enrolled at the London Film School, where she shifted her
focus from filmmaking to screenwriting before she graduated in 2016.
McPherson was then a principal director on the second and third seasons
of the children's show Apple Tree House, and she gained notice in
2018 for the script for her debut stage play, When The Lights Go
Out. During the Twenties, she directed episodes of programmes such
as EastEnders, Waterloo Road and Queenie, while
also serving as a second unit director on the Bridgerton spin-off
Queen Charlotte. McPherson next made the iconoclastic 2025
Doctor Who episode The Story &
The Engine, starring Ncuti Gatwa as the Fifteenth Doctor. She
has two children.

16.content:
Doctor Who season 15 is officially here, with the first episode dropping on BBC iPlayer for those eager to feast on all the timey wimey action the Doctor and his [new companion](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-belinda-mundy-flynn-exclusive-newsupdate/) have to offer.

Titled The Robot Revolution, the first episode introduces viewers to Belinda Chandra (Varada Sethu), who is kidnapped by robots from outer space! And in true Doctor Who fashion, the Doctor embarks on an intergalactic quest to get his new friend back home to Earth.

Alongside Sethu, season 15 will also feature the likes of Alan Cumming, Christopher Chung, Kadiff Kirwan and Charlie Condou - with details on some of their characters still tightly under wraps.

We also know that the new episodes will also feature the return of Ruby Sunday and [Susan Twist](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-susan-twist-return-confirmed-newsupdate/)'s character Susan Triad, plus a trip to the Interstellar Song Contest.

But what else do we know about Doctor Who season 15? Read on to find out more!

###### More like this

We now have a [confirmed release date](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-season-15-date-confirmed-newsupdate/) for Doctor Who season 15, with the first episode set to air on **on 12th April** on BBC One and BBC iPlayer.

Unlike last season, which saw episodes releasing on BBC iPlayer at midnight UK time, this season will see episodes arrive on the **streaming platform at 8am, before airing later that day on BBC One**.

This means season 15 airs just under a year after season 14, which debuted in May 2024.

In October 2023, it was announced that filming had started on Gatwa's second season.

#### Want to see this content?

We're not able to show you this content from Twitter. Please sign out of Contentpass to view this content.

Filming went on to conclude on 26th May 2024, with RTD writing on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/C7YjHpaN0cU/?utm_source=ig_embed&ig_rid=05398ee6-8ae3-4d0b-9dd7-184ae407e2f4): "That’s season 2 complete, well done everyone!"

**Who will star in Doctor Who season 15?**
------------------------------------------

Here are the cast members we currently know will be starring in Doctor Who season 15.

*   **Ncuti Gatwa as The Fifteenth Doctor**
*   **Millie Gibson as Ruby Sunday**
*   **Varada Sethu as Belinda Chandra**
*   **[Jonah Hauer-King](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-jonah-hauer-king-character/) as TBC**
*   **Jemma Redgrave as Kate Lethbridge-Stewart**
*   **Bonnie Langford as Melanie Bush**
*   **Ruth Madeley as Shirley Anne Bingham**
*   **Alexander Devrient as Colonel Ibrahim**
*   **Michelle Greenidge as Carla Sunday**
*   **Angela Wynter as Cherry Sunday**
*   **Anita Dobson as Mrs Flood**
*   **Susan Twist as Susan Triad**
*   **Alan Cumming as Mr Ring-a-Ding**
*   **Christopher Chung as Cassio**
*   **Kadiff Kirwan as TBC**
*   **Rose Ayling-Ellis as TBC**
*   **Benjamin Chivers as TBC**
*   **Charlie Condou as TBC**

Gatwa previously confirmed he would be staying for at least two seasons of Doctor Who, telling [Rolling Stone](https://www.rollingstone.co.uk/tv/ncuti-gatwa-interview-doctor-who-barbie-31011/): "\[Theatre\] kept me warm and it held me all night, even if I was broke. But I’m planning on getting back to it next year, after I finish season 2 of Doctor Who."

It's also been confirmed that Andor star Sethu has been cast as the Doctor's new companion, [Belinda Chandra](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-varada-sethu-character-newsupdate/), with new pictures of her being released after the 2024 Christmas special.

Sethu made her Doctor Who debut as Mundy Flynn in a guest role in the Steven Moffat-penned episode Boom – but her new character Belinda will be completely different.

**Read more:**

*   [Doctor Who first look confirms House of the Dragon star as mysterious new villain](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-freddie-fox-newsupdate/)
*   [Doctor Who's modern reboot could have been disastrous – here's how it defied the odds](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-modern-reboot-defied-odds-comment/)

![Image 1: Varada Sethu as Belinda Chandra in Doctor Who peering through a blind](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2024/12/504681-88e7a18.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Varada Sethu as Belinda Chandra in Doctor Who. BBC Studios/James Pardon

It's also been reported that [Gibson will take on a smaller role in season 15](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/millie-gibson-doctor-who-future-comment/) – something that could prove exciting as we'll get to see more of Ruby's life beyond her adventures with the Doctor.

This makes sense, given the ending of season 14 finale, Empire of Death. That episode's culmination saw Ruby find [her biological mother, Louise](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-ruby-mother-theories/), and on the brink of finding her biological father, William.

She decided to stay behind to get to know them and live her life back on Earth, but we know that she will be returning at some point in season 15, with Russell T Davies teasing more stories for Ruby and her family.

At San Diego Comic-Con, Davies subsequently confirmed that Ruby won't be settling down in season 15, and that she'll be suffering from post traumatic stress disorder in the new episodes, following her adventures in season 14.

![Image 2: Millie Gibson as Ruby Sunday and Jemma Redgrave as Kate Stewart in Doctor Who stood in a control room looking shocked](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2024/12/504679-dc2c324.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,443)

Millie Gibson as Ruby Sunday and Jemma Redgrave as Kate Stewart in Doctor Who. BBC Studios/James Pardon

Gibson and Jonah Hauer-King have also been spotted together filming on set, with the actor appearing to play a love interest of Ruby's. At Comic-Con, it was confirmed that [Hauer-King's character would be a part of Ruby's season 2 storyline](https://deadline.com/2024/07/doctor-who-jonah-hauer-king-nicola-coughlan-christmas-special-cast-1236023811/).

There have been more teases about who we can expect, too, including a [familiar face from an anniversary episode](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-season-15-returning-face-newsupdate/).

Script editor Scott Handcock previously wrote in Doctor Who Magazine: "A busy day for Block 2 as Ncuti Gatwa and Millie Gibson meet with writers for a Block 2 page turn ahead of an afternoon readthrough – that features an actor who might be familiar to Doctor Who fans having appeared in a previous anniversary adventure."

Plus, plenty of characters from season 14 will be carried through to the next season, including Ruby's family – adoptive mum Carla (played by [Michelle Greenidge](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-michelle-greenidge-ncuti-gatwa-exclusive-newsupdate/)) and nan [Cherry (played by Angela Wynter)](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-cherry-sunday-angela-wynter/).

![Image 3: Anita Dobson as Mrs. Flood in Doctor Who. She is wearing a dark coloured gilet and tanned shirt, with her hands crossed as she looks across at something with confusion.](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2024/05/anita-dobson-doctor-who-052541d.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Anita Dobson as Mrs Flood in Doctor Who. James Pardon/Bad Wolf/BBC Studios

One person we will also see again is Ruby's mysterious and all-knowing neighbour [Mrs Flood, played by Anita Dobson](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-mrs-flood-anita-dobson-explained/). We didn't get answers about her last season but we suspect more will come now.

Classic Doctor Who companion [Bonnie Langford](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-bonnie-langford-mel-return-the-giggle-newsupdate/) is also expected to return alongside other UNIT supporting players including Jemma Redgrave as Kate Lethbridge-Stewart and Alexander Devrient as Colonel Ibrahim.

Ruth Madeley has also been spotted filming as UNIT scientific advisor Shirley Anne Bingham, having been introduced in the 60th-anniversary episodes but being absent from season 14.

It is unknown if we can expect returns from Yasmin Finney as Rose Noble or Lenny Rush as Morris Gibbons.

![Image 4: Susan Twist wearing a white blouse and brown suit jacket, looking up.](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/02/susan-twist-06d3834.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Susan Twist. James Pardon/Bad Wolf/BBC Studios

With fans being treated to [a teaser trailer](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-season-15-trailer-newsupdate/) at the end of the Christmas special, Joy to the World, it was also recently confirmed that [Rose Ayling-Ellis](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-casts-rose-ayling-ellis-season-15-newsupdate/) will be among the guest stars for the next season, as she features in an "absolutely terrifying" upcoming episode.

Davies said of her casting: "We always want guest actors on Doctor Who to have fun, but Rose takes it to a whole new level. She storms in with an astonishing performance of terror, anger and bravery in one of the most frightening episodes we’ve ever made.”

The showrunner also recently told **Radio Times**: "There’s a lot of amazing guest stars we haven’t announced yet. Some great monsters, great settings every week. Mainly, you’ll have \[new companion\] Belinda, played by Varada Sethu, who’s gorgeous."

In February 2025, it was confirmed that [Christopher Chung](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-season-15-christopher-chung-first-look-newsupdate/) would be guest starring in the new season, playing a character called Cassio – but whether he is friend or foe remains to be seen.

Meanwhile, his [Slow Horses](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/slow-horses-season-6-renewal-newsupdate/) co-star [Kadiff Kirwan](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-kadiff-kirwan-casting-newsupdate/) was confirmed to have a role in March 2025.

When the release date for season 15 was officially confirmed, it was announced that Alan Cumming had joined the cast, although he will not be playing King James, who he played in season 11. Instead, he will voice cartoon character Mr Ring-a-Ding, who bursts from a movie screen in 1952 with terrifying consequences.

Meanwhile, The Devil's Hour star Benjamin Chivers was spotted in a trailer for the new season, and Charlie Condou was later announced as playing a new character.

**How many episodes will be in Doctor Who season 15?**
------------------------------------------------------

Doctor Who season 15 will consist of **eight episodes.**

Alex Pillai will be directing the first block of episodes, with [Peter Hoar](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-season-15-directors-peter-hoar-return-newsupdate/) helming the second.

Speaking to [RadioTimes.com](https://radiotimes.com/) and other press about [The Last of Us](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/last-of-us-tv-show-release-date/) in 2023, Hoar admitted that he "would love" to do another episode of the long-running sci-fi series – although he said that wasn't "on the cards" at the time.

![Image 5: Peter Hoar holding a BAFTA award.](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2023/01/Peter-Hoar-7f0e47c.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,466)

Director Peter Hoar. Getty

He added: "I was with \[Russell\] last night and someone asked the exact same question, 'Oh, does this mean you're going to do Doctor Who together?' and I said, 'No,' and you could tell nobody believed a word I was saying, but it's true. I grew up with Doctor Who, hence why I would do it again."

Other directors for the season include Amanda Brotchie, Ben A Williams, and Makalla McPherson.

Much like season 14, episodes will air on BBC One and will be be available internationally on [Disney Plus](https://www.radiotimes.com/technology/disney-plus-uk/).

The full list of episodes was confirmed in March 2025, with the rundown as follows:

*   **The Robot Revolution:** Written by Russell T Davies, directed by Peter Hoar
*   **Lux:** Written by Russell T Davies, directed by Amanda Brotchie
*   **The Well:** Written by Russell T Davies & Sharma Angel Walfall, directed by Amanda Brotchie
*   **Lucky Day:** Written by Pete McTighe, directed by Peter Hoar
*   **The Story & the Engine:** Written by Inua Ellams, directed by Makalla McPherson
*   **The Interstellar Song Contest:** Written by Juno Dawson, directed by Ben A Williams
*   **Wish World:** Written by Russell T Davies, directed by Alex Sanjiv Pillai
*   **The Reality War:** Written by Russell T Davies, directed by Alex Sanjiv Pillai

#### Want to see this content?

We're not able to show you this content from Squirrel. Please sign out of Contentpass to view this content.

**Who is writing for Doctor Who season 15?**
--------------------------------------------

Of course, showrunner **Russell T Davies**, who penned all three of the 60th anniversary specials and six of the eight episodes of the 14th season, has returned to write episodes in the 2025 run.

However, we've also got four new writers stepping in to write episodes in season 15: **Pete McTighe, Juno Dawson, Inua Ellams and Sharma Angel-Walfall**.

Returning Doctor Who writer McTighe said: "The TARDIS is my home away from home, so it's been a joy to step back inside, with Russell at the console and the incredible team at Bad Wolf hanging on for dear life.

#### Want to see this content?

We're not able to show you this content from Instagram. Please sign out of Contentpass to view this content.

"I love this show with all my heart, and am really proud of what we've been able to achieve with my next episode."

Dawson added: "I started watching Doctor Who with my grandma when I was 10 years old in the 1990s. From writing fan fiction for an audience of one to scripting the best TV show of all time is truly a dream come true.

"I can't wait for fans and newcomers to see the new season."

![Image 6: Russell T Davies holds a microphone while speaking on stage](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2024/08/russell-t-davies-78f9810.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Russell T Davies. Anthony Devlin/Getty Images for CityCo

Ellams said: "For as long as I can remember television, I've been a Doctor Who fan. I started watching when I was 10 in Nigeria. The show invited me to dream, to live beyond my reality.

"Getting to write for the show felt like touching God; it was blasphemously humbling and exciting, and I can’t wait to share my story with the world."

Angel-Walfall said: "I am buzzing to be a part of such an iconic show! I am a massive Russell T Davies fan, so it is a dream come true to be able to work alongside him, especially on a show that I love.

"It’s a real privilege to be a part of the Doctor Who family. I have loved every minute!"

**What could Doctor Who season 15 be about?**
---------------------------------------------

While plot details are currently thin on the ground, we can speculate based on the tidbits of news that have emerged, and based on the new trailer.

The trailer shows **Ruby Sunday joining UNIT,** and we're shown a new look at Mrs Flood (Anita Dobson) with opera glasses.

The new footage **also hints at the return of the villainous [Pantheon of Discord](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-pantheon-gods-trickster-explained/)**, with the Doctor warning of "forces beyond this universe" playing "deadly" games, with a cartoon - now known to be Mr Ring-a-Ding - shown climbing out of a screen at the cinema.

It seems likely that **the Doctor will meet Varada Sethu's companion at the start of season 15**, after a one-off adventure with Nicola Coughlan's character in the Christmas special, before reuniting with Ruby midway through the season, in a similar fashion to his storyline with Donna and Martha in season 4.

![Image 7: Varada Sethu as Belinda Chandra in Doctor Who in a green outfit in the TARDIS](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2024/12/503296-8c18044.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Varada Sethu as Belinda Chandra in Doctor Who. BBC Studios/James Pardon

Season 15 will also likely **see questions answered surrounding the mysterious Mrs Flood, and whether further threats await from the Pantheon of Discord.**

We know that Ayling-Ellis's episode will be "terrifying", so **season 15 could take a slightly darker turn.**

The final episode of season 14, Empire of Death, saw the Doctor defeat Sutekh, who seemingly perished for good. He and Ruby then used DNA tracking from 2046 to find Ruby's mum, who turned out to be an ordinary woman, a nurse who, when she was a teenager, left Ruby for fear she couldn't protect her from her step-father, who was "trouble".

![Image 8: Ncuti Gatwa in Doctor Who season 2 in a waistcoat in the TARDIS](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2024/12/ncuti-season-2-392feec-e1737979791359.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Ncuti Gatwa in Doctor Who. BBC

Armed with this knowledge, Ruby and the Doctor tracked down her mother, and she introduced herself. As they started bonding, forming a family unit with Carla and Cherry, and searching for Ruby's father William, the Doctor realised she would have to stay behind.

The two bid a tearful farewell and the Doctor went off on his own - however, Russell T Davies has already teased that the story of Ruby Sunday, and her new family unit, will continue.

**Is there a trailer for Doctor Who season 15?**
------------------------------------------------

**Yes!** Check out the teaser trailer for Doctor Who season 15 below:

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

| Ncuti Gatwa
 |
| --- |
| [![Image 1](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/Ncuti_Gatwa-65764.jpg/250px-Ncuti_Gatwa-65764.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ncuti_Gatwa-65764.jpg)Gatwa in 2024

 |
| Born | Mizero Ncuti Gatwa

  
15 October 1992 (age 33)  

[Nyarugenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyarugenge_District "Nyarugenge District"), Kigali, Rwanda



 |
| Citizenship | 

*   Rwanda
*   United Kingdom



 |
| Education | [Royal Conservatoire of Scotland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Conservatoire_of_Scotland "Royal Conservatoire of Scotland") ([BA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts")) |
| Occupation | Actor |
| Years active | 2013–present |

**Mizero Ncuti Gatwa**[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-1) (;[\[note 1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-7) born 15 October 1992) is a Rwandan-born Scottish actor who is best known for his [breakthrough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakthrough_role "Breakthrough role") role as Eric Effiong in [_Sex Education_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_Education_/(TV_series/) "Sex Education (TV series)") (2019–2023) and the [Fifteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor "Fifteenth Doctor") in _[Doctor Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who "Doctor Who")_ (2023–2025).[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-Scottish-8)[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-TNS-9) He began his career on stage at the [Dundee Repertory Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dundee_Repertory_Theatre "Dundee Repertory Theatre") and was nominated for an [Ian Charleson Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Charleson_Award "Ian Charleson Award") for his performance as [Mercutio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercutio "Mercutio") in a 2014 production of _[Romeo & Juliet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romeo_%26_Juliet "Romeo & Juliet")_ at [HOME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HOME_/(Manchester/) "HOME (Manchester)") arts centre.

Early life and education
------------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ncuti_Gatwa&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")\]

Mizero Ncuti Gatwa was born in [Nyarugenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyarugenge_District "Nyarugenge District"), [Kigali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kigali "Kigali"), Rwanda, on 15 October 1992.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-10)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-11) His father, Tharcisse Gatwa, from Rwanda's [Karongi District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karongi_District "Karongi District"), is a journalist.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-12)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-13)

Gatwa's family escaped from Rwanda during the [1994 genocide against the Tutsi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rwandan_genocide "Rwandan genocide") and settled in Scotland.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-Scottish-8)[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-TNS-9) They lived in [Oxgangs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxgangs "Oxgangs") in Edinburgh, and moved to [Dunfermline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunfermline "Dunfermline") when he was 15.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-Greenwood-2023-14) Gatwa attended [Boroughmuir High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boroughmuir_High_School "Boroughmuir High School") and [Dunfermline High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunfermline_High_School "Dunfermline High School") before moving to [Glasgow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glasgow "Glasgow") to study at the [Royal Conservatoire of Scotland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Conservatoire_of_Scotland "Royal Conservatoire of Scotland"), graduating with a Bachelor of Arts in Acting in 2013.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-15)[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-16) While studying, he worked at the [LGBTQ+ club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay_bar "Gay bar") The Polo Lounge, handing out flyers and later becoming a [go-go dancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go-go_dancing "Go-go dancing").[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-Greenwood-2023-14) The Conservatoire awarded him an honorary doctorate at the class of 2022 graduation ceremony.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-17)

### 2013–2022: Early stage work and breakthrough with _Sex Education_

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ncuti_Gatwa&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2013–2022: Early stage work and breakthrough with Sex Education")\]

[![Image 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ab/Ncuti_Gatwa%2C_Jan_2019_on_MTV_International_01.jpg/250px-Ncuti_Gatwa%2C_Jan_2019_on_MTV_International_01.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ncuti_Gatwa,_Jan_2019_on_MTV_International_01.jpg)

Gatwa in 2019

After graduating, Gatwa was granted a position in the [Dundee Repertory Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dundee_Repertory_Theatre "Dundee Repertory Theatre") acting graduation scheme where he performed in several productions including [David Greig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Greig_/(dramatist/) "David Greig (dramatist)")'s _Victoria_.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-18)[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-19)[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-20) Around this time, Gatwa was attacked by three strangers in the street who fractured his jaw; this was fixed with titanium.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-Greenwood-2023-14) He had a brief role in the 2014 sitcom _[Bob Servant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Servant "Bob Servant")_, which was also set and filmed in Dundee.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-BBCBobServant-21) In 2014, Gatwa received a Commendation at the [Ian Charleson Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Charleson_Awards "Ian Charleson Awards") for his 2014 performance of [Mercutio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercutio "Mercutio") in _[Romeo and Juliet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romeo_and_Juliet "Romeo and Juliet")_ at [Home, Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HOME_/(Manchester/) "HOME (Manchester)").

In 2015, he appeared in a supporting role in the [miniseries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miniseries "Miniseries") _Stonemouth_, an adaptation of the [2012 novel of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stonemouth "Stonemouth").[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-Review-2019-22) That same year, he performed in the [Kneehigh Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kneehigh_Theatre "Kneehigh Theatre")'s production of _[946: The Amazing Story of Adolphus Tips](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/946:_The_Amazing_Story_of_Adolphus_Tips "946: The Amazing Story of Adolphus Tips")_, which was adapted from [Michael Morpurgo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Morpurgo "Michael Morpurgo")'s _[The Amazing Story of Adolphus Tips](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Amazing_Story_of_Adolphus_Tips "The Amazing Story of Adolphus Tips")_, about a [large-scale rehearsal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exercise_Tiger "Exercise Tiger") for the [D-Day landings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D-Day_landings "D-Day landings") in 1944 that resulted in numerous fatalities.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-23)[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-24) Gatwa played [Demetrius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demetrius_/(A_Midsummer_Night%27s_Dream/) "Demetrius (A Midsummer Night's Dream)") in the 2016 production of _[A Midsummer Night's Dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Midsummer_Night%27s_Dream "A Midsummer Night's Dream")_ at [Shakespeare's Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakespeare%27s_Globe "Shakespeare's Globe") directed by [Emma Rice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Rice "Emma Rice").[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-25)[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-CBrown-26)

In May 2018, Gatwa was cast in the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") [comedy-drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy-drama "Comedy-drama") series _[Sex Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_Education_/(TV_series/) "Sex Education (TV series)")_ as Eric Effiong;[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-BBCBobServant-21) the show was released in 2019 and garnered critical acclaim.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-27) For five months prior to this casting, he had been [homeless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeless "Homeless") after running out of savings, and had [couch surfed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Couch_surfing "Couch surfing").[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-TNS-9)[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-28)[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-Harris-2020-29) Gatwa received praise for his portrayal of Eric from critics, particularly for how his character was not relegated to the cliché of "gay or Black best friend slash sidekick stock character".[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-vulture-30)[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-dazed-31) He has earned numerous accolades for the role, including a [BAFTA Scotland Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Scotland "BAFTA Scotland") for [Best Actor in Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Scotland "BAFTA Scotland") in 2020, and three [BAFTA Television Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Television_Award "BAFTA Television Award") nominations for [Best Male Comedy Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Award_for_Best_Male_Comedy_Performance "British Academy Television Award for Best Male Comedy Performance"), one in 2020, 2021 and 2022 consecutively.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-vulture-30)[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-dazed-31)[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-32)[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-33)[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-34)

In April 2022, Gatwa was cast in [Greta Gerwig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greta_Gerwig "Greta Gerwig")'s _[Barbie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbie_/(film/) "Barbie (film)")_.[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-35) He performed an excerpt of _[Romeo and Juliet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romeo_and_Juliet "Romeo and Juliet")_ with [Mei Mac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mei_Mac "Mei Mac") at the 2023 [Coronation Concert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronation_Concert "Coronation Concert"),[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-36) and topped the [_Radio Times's_ TV 100 power list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Times%27s_TV_100 "Radio Times's TV 100") the same year.[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-37)

### 2023–2025: _Doctor Who_

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ncuti_Gatwa&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2023–2025: Doctor Who")\]

[![Image 3](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b8/Ncuti_Gatwa_3_cropped.png/250px-Ncuti_Gatwa_3_cropped.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ncuti_Gatwa_3_cropped.png)

Ncuti Gatwa as the Fifteenth Doctor

In May 2022, it was announced that Gatwa had been cast in _[Doctor Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who "Doctor Who")_ as a new incarnation of the show's protagonist, [the Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Doctor "The Doctor"), succeeding [Jodie Whittaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Whittaker "Jodie Whittaker") in the role.[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-38) Gatwa, who was cast in February,[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-39) was the first[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-40) black actor to lead the series, the fourth Scottish actor, and the first actor born outside the United Kingdom to do so.[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-41)[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-42)[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-43)[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-Belam-2022-44)[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-45) He was expected to take over the role in the third and final of the [2022 specials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_/(2022_specials/) "Doctor Who (2022 specials)") in October 2022,[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-46) but the final [Thirteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteenth_Doctor "Thirteenth Doctor") story "[The Power of the Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Power_of_the_Doctor "The Power of the Doctor")" revealed that Gatwa would play the [Fifteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor "Fifteenth Doctor"), with [David Tennant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Tennant "David Tennant") (who had previously played the [Tenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenth_Doctor "Tenth Doctor")) returning to play the [Fourteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourteenth_Doctor "Fourteenth Doctor").[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-47)[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-48)

He debuted in "[The Giggle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Giggle "The Giggle")", the third of the [60th anniversary specials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_/(2023_specials/) "Doctor Who (2023 specials)"), on 9 December 2023,[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-49) and starred in his first full episode, "[The Church on Ruby Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Church_on_Ruby_Road "The Church on Ruby Road")" on Christmas Day 2023, which was followed by the show's [fourteenth series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_/(series_14/) "Doctor Who (series 14)").[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-50) His performance in _Doctor Who_ has earned praise from critics. Many writers for _[The Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Independent "The Independent")_ called Gatwa's acting "interstellar" and "mesmerising."[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-51)[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-52) Naina Bajekal of [_Time_ magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_/(magazine/) "Time (magazine)") believed that Gatwa was "bringing _Doctor Who_ into a new era."[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-53) [Mary McNamara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_McNamara "Mary McNamara") of _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ called Gatwa "an absolute delight" and wrote that his "unbridled exuberance makes this an easy sell and serves as a data bridge between new viewers and old."[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-54) He was nearly cast in the [Jesse Eisenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_Eisenberg "Jesse Eisenberg") film _[A Real Pain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Real_Pain "A Real Pain")_ as [Rwandan genocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rwandan_genocide "Rwandan genocide") survivor Eloge, but scheduling conflicts with _Doctor Who_ led to [Kurt Egyiawan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Egyiawan "Kurt Egyiawan") being cast in the role instead.[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-55)

In May 2025 following the broadcast of "[The Reality War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War "The Reality War")" it was confirmed Gatwa would leave his role as the Doctor. Gatwa starred in a total of 18 episodes across two seasons between 2023 and 2025. This made his tenure in the main role the second shortest to date of the series since its revival in 2005, ahead of [Christopher Eccleston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Eccleston "Christopher Eccleston") who played the [Ninth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ninth_Doctor "Ninth Doctor") for [one season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_1 "Doctor Who series 1").[\[55\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-56)

In November 2024, Gatwa appeared as Algernon Moncrieff in Max Webster's production of [Oscar Wilde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_Wilde "Oscar Wilde")'s _[The Importance of Being Earnest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Importance_of_Being_Earnest "The Importance of Being Earnest")_ in the Lyttleton Theatre at the [National Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Theatre,_London "National Theatre, London"), opposite [Hugh Skinner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Skinner "Hugh Skinner") and [Sharon D. Clarke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharon_D._Clarke "Sharon D. Clarke"), running until January 2025. The play was also broadcast to cinemas worldwide through [National Theatre Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Theatre_Live "National Theatre Live") from February 2025.[\[56\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-auto-57)

In April 2025, it was announced that Gatwa will star as [Christopher Marlowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Marlowe "Christopher Marlowe") opposite [Edward Bluemel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Bluemel "Edward Bluemel") as [William Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare") in the UK premiere of _[Born With Teeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Born_With_Teeth "Born With Teeth")_ by [Liz Duffy Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liz_Duffy_Adams "Liz Duffy Adams"), directed by [Daniel Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Evans_/(actor/) "Daniel Evans (actor)") and produced by the [Royal Shakespeare Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Shakespeare_Company "Royal Shakespeare Company") at the [Wyndham's Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyndham%27s_Theatre "Wyndham's Theatre"), in London's [West End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_End_theatre "West End theatre") from August 2025. On 2 May 2025, Gatwa was initially announced as the United Kingdom's spokesperson for the [Eurovision Song Contest 2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest_2025 "Eurovision Song Contest 2025"),[\[57\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-58) however he was later replaced by [Sophie Ellis-Bextor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Ellis-Bextor "Sophie Ellis-Bextor") due to "unforeseen circumstances."[\[58\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-59)

Gatwa [came out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Came_out "Came out") as [queer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queer "Queer") in an August 2023 interview with _[Elle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elle_/(magazine/) "Elle (magazine)")_ magazine, having previously avoided discussing his sexuality, despite popular speculation, for his "safety and mental health".[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-Mahanty-2023-60)[\[60\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-61)[\[61\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-Lewis-2023-62) In the interview, Gatwa noted that he preferred not to label himself, and that he had been inspired by both his work on _Sex Education_ and an encounter with a Rwandan woman at [Manchester Pride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_Pride "Manchester Pride") some years previously, having "never met another queer Rwandan person before."[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-Mahanty-2023-60) He later stated that he had "never been in the closet, you know. I just never talked about it. The work I do is what's important."[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-Greenwood-2023-14)[\[61\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-Lewis-2023-62)

In 2024, Gatwa responded to criticism of his casting in _Doctor Who_ because of his race, stating that "There's so much white mediocrity that gets celebrated, and Black people, we have to be absolutely flawless to get half of \[that\] anyway. So, I'm slowly training myself out of that and being like, 'No shit. You deserve love just for existing.'"[\[62\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-63)[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-64)[\[64\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa#cite_note-65)

May 12, 2025

The writer of the latest adventure discusses the importance of giving credit, the Fugitive Doctor, and the episode’s connection to Dot and Bubble…

In [_The Story & the Engine_](https://www.doctorwho.tv/stories/the-story-and-the-engine), the [Fifteenth Doctor](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/fifteenth-doctor) visits a barber shop in Lagos, Nigeria – a place where he has found a sense of community and belonging. This is a familiar theme for episode writer Inua Ellams, who is also known for his poetry and playwriting; including _Barber Shop Chronicles_.

We spoke to Inua about how he developed this story as both a native to Nigeria and long-time Doctor Who fan, the power of storytelling, and how _The Story & the Engine_ unexpectedly connects to some of the Doctor’s previous adventures…

_**The Story & the Engine**_ **is now streaming on BBC iPlayer in the UK and Disney+ where available.**

![Image 1: Inua Ellams on the set of 'The Story & the Engine'](https://cms.doctorwho.tv/sites/default/files/2025-05/body6-DWTV-Gallery-Module-Watermark-Template-a811382903.jpg)

Inua Ellams on the set of 'The Story & the Engine'.

**The Story & the Engine** _**explores identity, community and history all through the lens of storytelling. How did you develop the idea for this episode?**_

I had been wanting to write a Doctor Who story for some time, and Ncuti \[Gatwa\] wished for me to write one too! I had a much larger story idea, and Russell \[T Davies\]'s suggestion was, “How about something set in one location?” and so the barber shop idea came about from this. I think of story ideas as different logs in a fire, you know, just waiting – suddenly there was a spark, and it roared to flame.

This story sparked from something I read in lockdown which angered me, about uncredited artistic work. I initially thought about Anansi as a character - perhaps being the hive of all stories, but never credited for it. So that was loosely where the idea began to percolate. When I read stories of Anansi as a trickster figure, and how he sometimes treated his children, I developed the idea of a mortal being the one to lift up all the gods; and that's when I settled on [the Barber](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/the-barber) being the one carrying this hive of stories and never getting credited for that work.

![Image 2: The Story & the Engine](https://cms.doctorwho.tv/sites/default/files/2025-05/body3DWTV-Gallery-Module-Watermark-Template-d75cbce997.jpg)

The Doctor explores a market in Lagos in 'The Story & the Engine'.

_**The Doctor lands in Lagos in 2019. It’s rare for the series to visit the recent past, is there something about that year in particular that’s relevant to you or the story?**_

We were trying to create a story that was sort of in keeping with the world of my play, _Barber Shop Chronicles_, which was set around that time. The play is centered around different barber shops across Africa and the UK – so in my ‘Inua Ellams Cinematic Universe’, this is sort of a different story in a parallel world.

I like the idea that the Doctor’s adventure in the barber shop somehow ignites the events of the play in another world – but ultimately that’s not serious, just me playing 3D chess with myself and all my different characters!

_**Are there any influences or references to Nigerian culture or storytelling/folklore that Doctor Who fans may have missed in the episode?**_

We shot a much longer sequence near the end that we couldn’t fit in; where the Doctor and [Belinda](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/belinda-chandra) enter the Story Engine and find items, icons of all stories ever told, in the ship. The Story Engine operates much like the [TARDIS](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/the-tardis) – bigger than it seems! So there are icons for everything – we mention Hemingway, there are three of his books on the shelf. We see a plaque of a bronze from Benin City, my ancestral home in Nigeria. There are gingerbread men, references to Hansel & Gretel, _One Thousand and One Nights_ – talismans to every story ever told.

Amongst those are icons specific to West African folklore, but there’s also East African, Western, Scandinavian, Asian, Indian – everything, crammed into the Story Engine. I honestly couldn’t believe the amount of detail put into that set; it was like a candy store!

![Image 3: The Story & the Engine](https://cms.doctorwho.tv/sites/default/files/2025-05/body7DWTV-Gallery-Module-Watermark-Template-0fa8cbfe24.jpg)

The Barber (Ariyon Bakare) in his Story Engine.

**The Story & the Engine** _**also has big implications for the concept of Gods within the Whoniverse. Are there any other characters of folklore you think would make for a good Doctor Who story?**_

As Ncuti has said before, I’d really love there to be an Orisha story, where the Doctor meets the West African deities. I’d also really want him to spend some time in ancient China – they have something like two dozen thunder gods! Also the Ramayana, an epic from ancient India. My friend Vinay Patel dipped a bit into Indian history with the Partition in [_Demons of the Punjab_](https://www.doctorwho.tv/stories/demons-of-the-punjab), but I’d like the Doctor to meet some of the Hindu myths and legends, there’s so much there.

_**Jo Martin makes an exciting cameo as the**_ [_**Fugitive Doctor**_](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/fugitive-doctor)_**! How did this appearance come about?**_

This was Russell’s idea, and I fell deeply in love with it and wanted it to happen. We just get a brief glimpse into what the Doctor was doing while she was a fugitive, there’s still so much mystery surrounding that. And in an episode that features lots of Doctors, it’s a nice appetiser for the audience to remind them that there’s someone else here with a whole minefield of adventures and stories that we haven’t dipped into.

![Image 4: Jo Martin as the Fugitive Doctor](https://cms.doctorwho.tv/sites/default/files/2025-05/body2DWTV-Gallery-Module-Watermark-Template-2f1afae09a.jpg)

Jo Martin as the Fugitive Doctor in 'The Story & the Engine'.

_**As for the Fifteenth Doctor, this episode deals quite closely with his own sense of identity and community in Omo’s Palace. How was it to explore this side of the character?**_

I wrote this episode kind of ‘in conversation’ with Season 1’s [_Dot and Bubble_](https://www.doctorwho.tv/stories/dot-and-bubble), lots of people who have seen that episode get what it’s about. The Doctor’s anger and frustration at the end of that episode – it’s why he needs a place like the barber shop, but it is also why he feels so emotional about [Omo](https://www.doctorwho.tv/characters/omo-esosa)’s betrayal in the episode. It hits really deeply for him. I often want to suggest that people watch _Dot and Bubble_ and _The Story & the Engine_ back-to-back, to really understand what the Doctor is feeling here, his sense of need and what Lagos means to him.

The opening scene, when the Doctor walks through the market and is in utter joy – I cried when I saw the rushes, because it just clicked. It’s what I miss and love about returning to Nigeria – so understanding that need within the Doctor, and seeing it play out onscreen, was humbling.

_**As well as**_ **Barber Shop Chronicles**_**, do you have any recommended stories or media for Doctor Who fans who loved this episode?**_

I wrote a book of poems called _The Actual_, and there are a couple of poems inside that book that my episode references. They’re recommended for adults as they contain strong language, but those were spinning in my head when I was writing _The Story & the Engine_.

I mention the TARDIS in one, and reference _Back to the Future_ and the quantum realm – that one’s about the birth of hip-hop, but also its relationship with West African symbolism. If you can find those poems, you might be able to read some of the seeds of my episode.

* * *

_**The Story & the Engine**_ **is now streaming on BBC iPlayer in the UK and Disney+ where available.**

[MBE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_British_Empire "Order of the British Empire") [FRSL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fellow_of_the_Royal_Society_of_Literature "Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature")
