[Jos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos "Jos"), [Plateau State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plateau_State "Plateau State"), [Nigeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria "Nigeria")



 |
| Citizenship | Nigeria |
| Education | [Firhouse Community College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firhouse_Community_College "Firhouse Community College"), [Dublin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dublin "Dublin"), [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland "Ireland") |
| Occupations | Poet, playwright |
| Known for | _Barber Shop Chronicles_ |
| Awards | [Edinburgh Fringe First Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fringe_First "Fringe First") (2008) |
| Website | [www.inuaellams.com](http://www.inuaellams.com/) |

**Inua Marc Mohammed Onore de Ellams II**[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-CV-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-Website-2) [MBE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_British_Empire "Order of the British Empire") [FRSL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fellow_of_the_Royal_Society_of_Literature "Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature")[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-RSL-3) (born 23 October 1984)[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-CV-1) is a Nigerian-born British poet, playwright and performer. He was appointed [Member of the Order of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire "Member of the Order of the British Empire") (MBE) in the [2023 Birthday Honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Birthday_Honours "2023 Birthday Honours") for services to the arts.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-4)

Early years and education
-------------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Inua_Ellams&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early years and education")\]

Inua Ellams was born in 1984 in [Jos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos "Jos"), [Plateau State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plateau_State "Plateau State"), Nigeria, to a Muslim father and a Christian mother.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-NYT_2020-5) When he was 12 years old, he moved with his family to England, and three years later to Ireland, where he attended [Firhouse Community College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firhouse_Community_College "Firhouse Community College").[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-Irish_Times_2017-6)

Ellams has written for the [Royal Shakespeare Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Shakespeare_Company "Royal Shakespeare Company"),[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-BBC-16-05-7) [Royal National Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_National_Theatre "Royal National Theatre") and the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC").

In June 2018, Ellams was elected as a Fellow of the [Royal Society of Literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Society_of_Literature "Royal Society of Literature") as part of its _40 Under 40_ initiative.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-RSL-3)[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-RSL-18-06-8) He took part in [The Complete Works](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Complete_Works_/(poetry/) "The Complete Works (poetry)") mentoring programme for poets of colour.

*   _Thirteen Fairy Negro Tales_ ([flipped eye publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flipped_eye_publishing "Flipped eye publishing"), 2004)
*   _Candy Coated Unicorns and Converse All Stars_ (flipped eye publishing, 2010)
*   _The Wire-Headed Heathen_ ([Akashic Books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akashic_Books "Akashic Books"), 2015)

#### Featured in anthologies

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Inua_Ellams&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Featured in anthologies")\]

*   _The Salt Book of Younger Poets_ ([Salt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt_Publishing "Salt Publishing"), 2010)[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-Inua_Ellams_%E2%80%93_Poetry_Spotlight-9)
*   _The Valley Press Anthology of Prose Poetry_ (Valley Press, 2018)\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\]
*   _Ten: The New Wave_ ([Bloodaxe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloodaxe_Books "Bloodaxe Books"), 2013)[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-Inua_Ellams_%E2%80%93_Poetry_Spotlight-9)

### Performances and plays

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Inua_Ellams&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Performances and plays")\]

Ellams's one-man show _The 14th Tale_ was awarded an [Edinburgh Fringe First](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburgh_Fringe_First "Edinburgh Fringe First") at the [Edinburgh International Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburgh_International_Festival "Edinburgh International Festival") in 2009, and later transferred to the Royal National Theatre, London.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-BritishCouncil-10)

A one-man show staged at the [Soho Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soho_Theatre "Soho Theatre") in 2010,[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-BTG-10-11) telling the story of twins born on Nigeria's independence day.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-Guardian-10-10-12)

#### _Barber Shop Chronicles_

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Inua_Ellams&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Barber Shop Chronicles")\]

_Barber Shop Chronicles_ is a play set in black [barber shops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barber "Barber") in six cities on one day, against the backdrop of a football match between [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") and [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona"). The play explores the [African diaspora in the UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_British "Black British"),[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-BBC-17-11-13) masculinity, homosexuality and religion. The play was produced by the National Theatre, Fuel Theatre and [Leeds Playhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeds_Playhouse "Leeds Playhouse") and was shortlisted for the [Alfred Fagon Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Fagon_Award "Alfred Fagon Award") in 2017.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-AlfredFagon-14) Following a period of touring, the play was also performed at the [Roundhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roundhouse_/(venue/) "Roundhouse (venue)") in 2019,[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-Guardian-19-07-15) and a recording of the National Theatre production was streamed in May 2020 as part of the _National Theatre at Home_ season.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-Guardian-20-05-16) For the production, Ellams recorded 60 hours of "male banter"[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-ES-19-07-17) in barbershops all over Africa and in London at his barber Peter's shop _Emmanuel's_ in [Clapham Junction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clapham_Junction_/(area/) "Clapham Junction (area)").[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-ES-19-07-17) This project originally did not secure funding.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-Wildness-17-10-18)

#### _An Evening with an Immigrant_

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Inua_Ellams&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: An Evening with an Immigrant")\]

At the [Traverse Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traverse_Theatre "Traverse Theatre"), Edinburgh, in 2017, Ellams performed a live stage programme titled _An Evening with an Immigrant_, with anecdotes of his childhood and his experiences as a refugee.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-Guardian-17-08-19) An excerpt was shown at the [Hay Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hay_Festival "Hay Festival") on 24 May 2020.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-BritishCouncil-10)[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-Hay-20-05-20)

#### _The Half God of Rainfall_

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Inua_Ellams&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: The Half God of Rainfall")\]

In April 2019, his new play, _The Half God of Rainfall_, was presented at the [Birmingham Repertory Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham_Repertory_Theatre "Birmingham Repertory Theatre"),[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-BRT-19-04-21) in advance of its run at London's [Kiln Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiln_Theatre "Kiln Theatre"), as well as its publication as a book.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-Guardian-19-04-22)

In December 2019–February 2020, a reworking by Ellams of [Chekhov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anton_Chekhov "Anton Chekhov")'s play _[Three Sisters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three_Sisters_/(play/) "Three Sisters (play)")_ was performed at the Royal National Theatre, London.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-TimeOut-19-12-23) The play restaged the story in the 1960s in the midst of the [Biafran war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biafran_war "Biafran war") in Nigeria.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-FT-19-03-24)

In January 2025, it was announced that Ellams had joined the writing team of the [fifteenth series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15 "Doctor Who series 15") of _[Doctor Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who "Doctor Who")_.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-25)[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-26) Ellams is the first black man to have written for the television series, and the fourth black writer overall (after [Malorie Blackman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malorie_Blackman "Malorie Blackman"), [Charlene James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlene_James "Charlene James") and Sharma Angel Walfall).

Ellams wrote the episode _[The Story & the Engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Story_%26_the_Engine "The Story & the Engine")_, set in contemporary Lagos, Nigeria, which was broadcast on 10 May 2025.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-27)

*   2008: winner of an [Edinburgh Fringe First Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fringe_First "Fringe First") for _The 14th Tale_.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-Stage-17-03-28)
*   2014: Live Canon International Poetry Prize.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-BritishCouncil-10)[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-TheBreak-29)
*   2017: shortlisted for the [Alfred Fagon Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Fagon_Award "Alfred Fagon Award"), for _The Barber Shop Chronicles_.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-AlfredFagon-14)
*   2018: elected a Fellow of the [Royal Society of Literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Society_of_Literature "Royal Society of Literature").[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inua_Ellams#cite_note-RSL-18-06-8)
*   2020: winner of the medal for Poetry at the [Hay Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hay_Festival "Hay Festival") for _The Half God of Rainfall_ and for _The Barber Shop Chronicles_,

**Belinda Chandra** is a fictional character in the [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_in_the_United_Kingdom "Television in the United Kingdom") [science fiction television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_fiction_television "Science fiction television") series _[Doctor Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who "Doctor Who")_, portrayed by [Varada Sethu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu "Varada Sethu"). The character was created by _Doctor Who_ showrunner [Russell T Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell_T_Davies "Russell T Davies"). In the show's [fifteenth series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15 "Doctor Who series 15"), Belinda serves as the [companion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Companion_/(Doctor_Who/) "Companion (Doctor Who)") to the [Fifteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor "Fifteenth Doctor") ([Ncuti Gatwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa "Ncuti Gatwa")), an incarnation of the [alien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extraterrestrial_life "Extraterrestrial life") [time traveller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_travel_in_fiction "Time travel in fiction") known as [the Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Doctor "The Doctor"). Debuting in the 2025 episode "[The Robot Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Robot_Revolution "The Robot Revolution")", Belinda is initially kidnapped by robots from another planet, and after the Doctor saves her, the pair find they cannot return to her home time period on Earth. She travels with the Doctor to use a device called the [Vindicator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vindicator_/(Doctor_Who/) "Vindicator (Doctor Who)") in order to return home. She eventually returns home but is trapped within a [heteronormative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heteronormative "Heteronormative") alternate reality created by the Doctor's enemy [The Rani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rani "The Rani"), in which Belinda has had a daughter named [Poppy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poppy_/(Doctor_Who/) "Poppy (Doctor Who)") with the Doctor. After Poppy is removed from the timeline alongside the reality, the Doctor restores Poppy to the timeline as Belinda's daughter, and she remains on Earth to care for her.

Sethu had previously portrayed the character Mundy Flynn in the 2024 episode "[Boom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boom_/(Doctor_Who/) "Boom (Doctor Who)")". Davies was impressed with Sethu's performance and after discussion with the production team, she was offered the role of Belinda without needing to audition. Unlike other companions in the series, Belinda was portrayed as someone who did not want to partake in the Doctor's adventures and wishes to return home, providing friction between the two characters.

Belinda received a positive response for her appearance in her debut episode, "The Robot Revolution", with many critics positively highlighting her unique dynamic with the Doctor. The conclusion of her arc and her role in the season finale, "[The Reality War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War "The Reality War")", was criticised by critics, with many feeling that Belinda was "wasted" as a character.

_[Doctor Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who "Doctor Who")_ is a long-running British [science-fiction television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_fiction_on_television "Science fiction on television") series that began in 1963. It stars its protagonist, [The Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Doctor "The Doctor"), an alien who travels through time and space in a ship known as the [TARDIS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TARDIS "TARDIS"), as well as their travelling [companions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Companion_/(Doctor_Who/) "Companion (Doctor Who)").[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-1) When the Doctor dies, they can undergo a process known as "[regeneration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regeneration_/(Doctor_Who/) "Regeneration (Doctor Who)")", completely changing the Doctor's appearance and personality.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-2) Throughout their travels, the Doctor often comes into conflict with various [alien species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Doctor_Who_universe_creatures_and_aliens "List of Doctor Who universe creatures and aliens") and antagonists.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-:422-3)[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-4)

Belinda first appears in the 2025 episode "[The Robot Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Robot_Revolution "The Robot Revolution")". Several years before the episode's events, she received a star diploma from her ex-boyfriend, Alan Budd (Jonny Green). This diploma resulted in a planet orbiting the star to be dubbed "Missbelindachandra One". In May 2025, she works as a nurse and lives in a [sharehome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharehome "Sharehome"). Robots from Missbelindachandra One kidnap her and take her to the planet, dubbing her the Queen of the planet. They attempt to marry her to the "[AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence") Generator", the overlord of the planet, but the [Fifteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor "Fifteenth Doctor") ([Ncuti Gatwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa "Ncuti Gatwa")) saves her. The pair are recaptured, and it is revealed the Generator is actually Alan, who had been kidnapped by the robots many years prior. Belinda and the Doctor work together to stop Alan, and prepare to leave. The Doctor, remembering her descendant [Mundy Flynn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mundy_Flynn "Mundy Flynn"), who he worked with in the far future (as seen in the 2024 episode "[Boom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boom_/(Doctor_Who/) "Boom (Doctor Who)")"), attempts to get her to travel with him, but she rejects him and insists he take her home. The Doctor obliges but cannot return to the time period from which Belinda hailed. In the following episode, "[Lux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lux_/(Doctor_Who/) "Lux (Doctor Who)")" (2025), the Doctor constructs a device called the [Vindicator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vindicator_/(Doctor_Who/) "Vindicator (Doctor Who)"), which will allow them to return to May 2025 when enough locations across time and space have been visited. The following episodes depict the Doctor and Belinda travelling across the universe to gain enough energy on the Vindicator to return home.

The Vindicator eventually gathers enough energy to return home at the end of "[The Interstellar Song Contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Interstellar_Song_Contest "The Interstellar Song Contest")" (2025), but the pair wind up trapped in an alternate, [heteronormative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heteronormativity "Heteronormativity") reality created by the Doctor's enemy [The Rani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rani "The Rani") ([Archie Panjabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Panjabi "Archie Panjabi") and [Anita Dobson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anita_Dobson "Anita Dobson")). The Doctor and Belinda are reimagined in this reality as a married couple who have an infant daughter named Poppy (Sienna-Robyn Mavanga-Phipps), with no memories of their old lives. The Doctor is eventually able to recover his memories and also restores Belinda's. When he goes to confront the Rani and dispel the altered reality, Belinda is placed inside of a special room alongside Poppy in order to prevent Poppy from being erased when the reality is dispelled. When reality is restored, Poppy is still erased from both of their memories, but after the Doctor is reminded of Poppy's existence, he causes a regeneration in the time vortex. This results in reality changing to have Belinda be Poppy's mother, but not the Doctor's child. Belinda stays behind to care for Poppy while the Doctor departs to regenerate.

Belinda, outside of the television series, also appears in comic strips published by [Titan Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titan_Comics "Titan Comics"),[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-5) as well as in several novels.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-6)

Creation and development
------------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Belinda_Chandra&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Creation and development")\]

[Varada Sethu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu "Varada Sethu") was announced to be portraying a new companion in _[Doctor Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who "Doctor Who")_'s [fifteenth series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15 "Doctor Who series 15") in April 2024,[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-7) though the character she was playing was not announced prior to the 2024 [San Diego Comic-Con](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Comic-Con "San Diego Comic-Con"), where the character's name was confirmed.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-8) Prior to Sethu's appearance as Belinda, she appeared as the character Mundy Flynn in the 2024 episode "[Boom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boom_/(Doctor_Who/) "Boom (Doctor Who)")"; this episode aired after she had been confirmed as a companion, and her appearance in "Boom" was not confirmed prior to the episode's airing. The relationship between Flynn and Belinda was not established in the episode, leading to speculation of the two characters' relation. Prior to Flynn's appearance, the concept of a companion's actor appearing as different characters prior to the companion's introduction had previously been done with [Clara Oswald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clara_Oswald "Clara Oswald") ([Jenna Coleman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Coleman "Jenna Coleman")) in the show's [seventh series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_7 "Doctor Who series 7").[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-9)

Sethu was contacted to appear as Belinda shortly after portraying Flynn.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-:0-10) Though many actors had auditioned for the role of Belinda,[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-:1-11) showrunner [Russell T Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell_T_Davies "Russell T Davies") had greatly enjoyed Sethu's performance in "Boom", and when he pitched the idea of bringing her back, many involved in production quickly agreed, resulting in her not needing to audition for the part.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-12) The production team called Sethu in to explain the part, and told her at the end of the meeting that the part was hers, with Sethu quickly agreeing to portray Belinda.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-:1-11) Sethu's introduction as a companion makes her pairing with [Fifteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor "Fifteenth Doctor") actor [Ncuti Gatwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa "Ncuti Gatwa") the first time in _Doctor Who_ history that the main cast of a series was portrayed by an entirely person of colour cast.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-13)

Belinda, unlike prior companions, does not wish to travel with the Doctor and instead wants to return to her own life.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-:0-10) In an interview with _[Polygon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygon_/(website/) "Polygon (website)")_, Davies explained that Belinda's introduction was intended to "expand the range" of the show, citing that unlike the younger and more optimistic [Ruby Sunday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruby_Sunday "Ruby Sunday") ([Millie Gibson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millie_Gibson "Millie Gibson")) who had been the prior season's companion, Belinda had a different approach in that she saw the Doctor as someone "mad" and "dangerous".[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-:2-14) Sethu also explained that Belinda held the Doctor "accountable", and that she did not "put him on a pedestal", which she believed would make the dynamic feel refreshing for fans of the series.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-:0-10) In her debut episode, Belinda criticises the Doctor for testing her [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA "DNA") without permission,[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-:4-15) and sees the Doctor's lifestyle as increasingly dangerous and concerning as he tries to convince her to come with him.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-:5-16) Sethu said that this different relationship was unique for the fact it provided friction between the Doctor and Belinda, and that, throughout the season, it provided the opportunity for both characters to grow and understand the other for who they are.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-:2-14) Ncuti Gatwa, who portrayed the Fifteenth Doctor, stated that the relationship depicted on-screen was emblematic of the relationship he and Sethu had in real life as being equals.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-:2-14) The two built a strong off-camera friendship, which according to them bled through into the performance of both characters.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-:0-10)

Following her first appearance in "The Robot Revolution", Belinda was highly praised by critics, with many positively highlighting her dynamic with the Doctor and the potential her character had throughout the season.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-17)[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-18)[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-19) Sam Moore from _[Digital Spy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Spy "Digital Spy")_ believed that Belinda's "grounded" personality allowed her to feel like "a complete person" that echoed strong traits of several past companions in the series, such as [Rose Tyler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_Tyler "Rose Tyler") ([Billie Piper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Piper "Billie Piper")) and [Donna Noble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donna_Noble "Donna Noble") ([Catherine Tate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catherine_Tate "Catherine Tate")). Moore believed that this human touch allowed the audience to relate to and be engaged with her character.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-20) Alex Zalban, writing for _[GamesRadar+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GamesRadar%2B "GamesRadar+")_, highlighted her introduction as being one of the most surprising in the series, as the scene in which the Doctor and Belinda meet was stated to be "unsettling"; unlike other companion introductions, it provided a flip in the dynamic of the series that made viewers want the Doctor to take her home, instead of take her on adventures like with their other companions.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-:5-16) _[/Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki//Film "/Film")_'s Michael Boyle similarly opined that this take allowed for a more unique dynamic, as it brought out emotions and relationships not normally seen between the Doctor and their companion.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-:4-15) _[Gizmodo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gizmodo "Gizmodo")_'s James Whitbrook highlighted the dynamic the pairing of the Doctor and Belinda had, stating that Belinda's willingness to push back against the Doctor and disagree with him helped to make their relationship compelling with viewers. Whitbrook also highlighted how the pair were allowed to develop their relationship on-screen, unlike with [Ruby Sunday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruby_Sunday "Ruby Sunday") ([Millie Gibson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millie_Gibson "Millie Gibson")), the prior season's companion, whose relationship with the Doctor developed off-screen.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-21)

The resolution to Belinda's character arc in "The Reality War" led to criticism from critics.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-GR+-22)[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-IGN-23)[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-:3-24) Stefen Mohamed, writing for _[Den of Geek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Den_of_Geek "Den of Geek")_, felt that Belinda had become side-lined as a character in the episode, additionally feeling the episode overshadowed her in favour of focusing on Ruby's arc.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-:3-24) Writing for _[GamesRadar+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GamesRadar%2B "GamesRadar+")_, Will Salmon felt that Belinda's arc was "fumbled", feeling that its ending made it so her character was defined "by the actions of toxic men".[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-GR+-22) In a later piece for _[Gizmodo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gizmodo "Gizmodo")_, Whitbrook criticised the usage of Belinda's character by the end of the season, as he believed Belinda's character became more generic and sidelined as the season went on, falling into traditional companion archetypes instead of displaying the traits that had made her stand out in "The Robot Revolution". He further criticised Belinda's characterisation in "The Reality War", believing it to have regressed Belinda's character to solely being a mother caring for Poppy, which Whitbrook believed wasted her character arc.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-25) Sethu responded to criticism of the character's departure, opining that "it's a bit unfair because I think the writing was beautiful. I think it was tied up in a way that was perfect, I cannot think of a better way of completing that circle."[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra#cite_note-26)

[### It had a good run](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt31433814/reviews/?featured=rw10560910&ref_=tt_ururv_genai_c_1_hd)

I don't have all that much to add to the discourse except to point out that the "old" Doctor Who is currently rated 8.5, while the "new" Doctor Who is rated 6.2. This is not a coincidence. And that's taking into account a few not terribly great seasons at the tail end of the 2005 version.  
  
There are glimmers of Doctor Who within this travesty, but they mainly serve to torment fans with what might have been.  
  
The writing of late, is of such quality that I would not have been surprised if it had been revealed that it was created by LLMs. I have one episode left to go. I hear it will bring back an old friend. I shall watch it for that, raise a glass in toast, and wish the show farewell. The production is still great, the actors fabulous, the writing terrible. Unfortunately, as video games live or die based on gameplay, TV shows live or die based on writing. It's time to lay this one to rest.

[duncancmccann](https://www.imdb.com/user/ur28508955/?ref_=tt_ururv_genai_c_2_uname)

[### I tried.](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt31433814/reviews/?featured=rw9808808&ref_=tt_ururv_genai_c_2_hd)

Four episodes in and I had high hopes of the new series after the specials and Tennant reminding us of who The Doctor should be.  
  
I don't either hate or love the nu-nu-who, I'm just indifferent, I don't care anymore.  
  
It feels like a long-term relationship where gradually you realise that the two of you have grown apart. No matter how much you try, how much you want to make it work, the spark is gone.  
  
I don't feel it's the fault of the actors, it's the overall approach to the show. If RTD and Disney are trying for a whole new younger fan-base then maybe they'll get it - I wouldn't know, I'm too old 'my' Doctor was Tom Baker, of the reboot Doctors it's between Tennant and Smith, probably with Smith just edging it.  
  
I think it's time for me to end my love affair with Dr Who, there will always be a place in my heart for it and I may even occasionally visit but my feelings of commitment and connection have gone. I hope you find a new lover Doctor, someone that loves you as you are now. Don't worry about me Doctor I'll be fine, we had a great time together but it's time for me to move on - or perhaps I'll stay single and just reminice about the old days with Tom and Jon on the iPlayer while sobbing gently and considering getting an 11th cat.  
  
I don't think anything can replace you, so I'll be better on my own, it's sad but these things happen. All the best for the future eh? Oh and by the way, I'm keeping K9.

The story is pointless, flat, contradictory, boring and embarrassing. The healing and wise Doctor known as the preserver of values, life and the saviour of the Earth and the universe has mutated into a leading figure in a third-rate Punch and Judy show. Just as the Doctor has completely lost his grandeur and wisdom, the story has lost its brilliance. Where has the genius gone that in the series' heyday manifested itself in brilliant speeches, in exposing social and societal inequalities (when he uncovered the Ood scandal, for example) and ultimately through the wit, charm, cleverness and compassion of the main character? | Years active | 1990–present |
| Television | 

*   _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctors_/(2000_TV_series/) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_
*   _[Good Omens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Omens_/(TV_series/) "Good Omens (TV series)")_
*   _[Carnival Row](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnival_Row "Carnival Row")_
*   _[His Dark Materials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/His_Dark_Materials "His Dark Materials")_



 |

**Ariyon Bakare** ([Listen](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/8/82/Yo-Ariyon_Bakare.ogg/Yo-Ariyon_Bakare.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Yo-Ariyon_Bakare.ogg "File:Yo-Ariyon Bakare.ogg")) (born 1971) is an English actor, writer and director. He is known for his extensive work across theatre, television, and film.

In 1998, he became the first Black man to play a lead role in a BBC period drama, portraying Mehuru in the BAFTA-nominated miniseries A Respectable Trade. His performance was described by The Guardian as “powerful and understated… conveying dignity, intellect, and the quiet fury of a man surviving under unimaginable constraint.” Bakare’s portrayal marked a significant moment in British television history. He has since built a prolific career with major roles in Doctors, His Dark Materials, Carnival Row, Thirteen, Karen Pirie, Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell, and Mr Loverman. In 2025, he won the BAFTA TV Award for Best Supporting Actor for his role in Mr Loverman.

Bakare has also directed for television, received development funding from the UK Film Council for his debut feature Kodak Cowboy, and founded the racial justice initiative iC4RE. He is a long-time ambassador for WaterAid and delivered a keynote speech at St James’s Palace in 2025 on global water access and social justice.

Early life and education
------------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ariyon_Bakare&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")\]

Ariyon Bakare was born around 1971, of a Nigerian father. Growing up, he lived all around [east London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_London "East London"). Due to conflict with his father, Bakare left his family home at the age of 15, and completed his education while homeless for a year. He was close to his stepmother.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariyon_Bakare#cite_note-Biography-1)

Six months after returning home and reconciling with his father, at the age of 17, Bakare moved from [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") to [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") to pursue dance as a career. He trained as dancer at various conservatories, including [Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alvin_Ailey_American_Dance_Theater "Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater"). Two years into his training, he was informed that dancers often retire at a young age. The next day, he gave dance up, and began focusing on acting. He moved back to London at the age of 20, and began studying acting at [Drama Centre London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_Centre_London "Drama Centre London").[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariyon_Bakare#cite_note-Biography-1)

His first professional job was with the [Royal Shakespeare Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Shakespeare_Company "Royal Shakespeare Company") (RSC). He stated that while performing with the RSC, he also worked on jobs in [Scotland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scotland "Scotland"), as well as learning scriptwriting and singing soul and opera music.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariyon_Bakare#cite_note-Biography-1)

### Film and television

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ariyon_Bakare&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Film and television")\]

Bakare’s breakout television role came in 1998 when he played Mehuru in A Respectable Trade, a four-part BBC miniseries based on the novel by Philippa Gregory. His portrayal of an enslaved African intellectual navigating 18th-century British society was described by The Guardian as “powerful and understated… conveying dignity, intellect, and the quiet fury of a man surviving under unimaginable constraint.” The role marked the first time a Black man led a BBC period drama.

From 2001 to 2005, he starred as Dr. [Ben Kwarme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Kwarme "Ben Kwarme") in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_One "BBC One") soap opera _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctors_/(2000_TV_series/) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariyon_Bakare#cite_note-2) a role that earned him a Royal Television Society Midlands nomination for Best Actor in 2005.

After leaving _Doctors_, Bakare returned to direct and write several episodes. He then co-wrote and starred in the Channel 4 drama _Stealing Lives_. In November 2008, he appeared as a villain in the BBC drama _[Spooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spooks_/(TV_series/) "Spooks (TV series)")_, and in October 2009, he made an appearance in _[Casualty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casualty_/(TV_series/) "Casualty (TV series)")_.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariyon_Bakare#cite_note-3)

In 2011, Bakare played a mini-cab driver, Carl Lucas, in the last episode of the sixth series of _[Law & Order UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_%26_Order_UK "Law & Order UK")_, first broadcast in 2012. He appeared in _[Dancing on the Edge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancing_on_the_Edge_/(TV_series/) "Dancing on the Edge (TV series)")_, first broadcast in 2013, as Wesley Holt, a band manager. Bakare later appeared in _[Doctor Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who "Doctor Who")_, in the 2015 episode, "[The Woman Who Lived](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Woman_Who_Lived "The Woman Who Lived")", alongside [Maisie Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maisie_Williams "Maisie Williams"). He played the antagonist of the episode, a lion-like creature called Leandro.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariyon_Bakare#cite_note-4)

He appeared as a Rebel pilot in _[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogue_One:_A_Star_Wars_Story "Rogue One: A Star Wars Story")_. In 2019, he began appearing in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") TV series _[His Dark Materials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/His_Dark_Materials_/(TV_series/) "His Dark Materials (TV series)")_, in the role of [Lord Boreal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_His_Dark_Materials_and_The_Book_of_Dust_characters#Lord_Boreal "List of His Dark Materials and The Book of Dust characters").[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariyon_Bakare#cite_note-Biography-1)

In 2022 He played the older version of character Alex Gilrey who is a long term murder suspect in the BBC TV mini series Karen Pirie which was based on the Inspector Karen Pirie series by Val McDermid.\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\]

Bakare's theatre credits include productions at the [RSC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Shakespeare_Company "Royal Shakespeare Company") and the [Lyric Hammersmith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyric_Theatre_/(Hammersmith/) "Lyric Theatre (Hammersmith)"). He played Florindo in [Tim Supple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Supple "Tim Supple")'s staging of _[A Servant to Two Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Servant_of_Two_Masters "Servant of Two Masters")_ at the [Young Vic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Vic "Young Vic") theatre.\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\]

He starred opposite [Janet Suzman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Suzman "Janet Suzman") in the British premiere of _Dream of the Dog_, where he played a South African nattily-clad architect, "Look Smart".[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariyon_Bakare#cite_note-5)

Awards and nominations
----------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ariyon_Bakare&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Awards and nominations")\]

For his role in _Doctors_, Bakare was nominated for [Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Actor "British Soap Award for Best Actor") at the [2004 British Soap Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_British_Soap_Awards#2004_winners "The British Soap Awards").[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariyon_Bakare#cite_note-6)

In 2005, he was nominated for Best Actor at the [Royal Television Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Television_Society "Royal Television Society") (RTS) Midlands Awards for his portrayal of Dr. Ben Kwarme in the BBC series _Doctors_.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariyon_Bakare#cite_note-7)

He received a commendation at the [Ian Charleson Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Charleson_Awards "Ian Charleson Awards") for his role as Florindo in _[A Servant to Two Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Servant_of_Two_Masters "Servant of Two Masters")_ at the Young Vic.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariyon_Bakare#cite_note-8)\[_[circular reference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Wikipedia_and_sources_that_mirror_or_use_it "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_\]

Bakare also received multiple Best Actor awards for his performance in the short film _Waiting for Time_ (2019), including:

*   \*\*Best Actor in a Short Film\*\* – Wild Indie Sci-Fi & Fantasy Film Festival (2020)[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariyon_Bakare#cite_note-9)
*   \*\*Best Actor\*\* – Overcome Film Festival (2020)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariyon_Bakare#cite_note-10)
*   \*\*Best Actor\*\* – IndieFest Film Awards (2020)\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\]
*   \*\*Best Actor\*\* – European Cinematography Awards (2020)\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\]
*   \*\*Best Actor\*\* – Five Continents International Film Festival (2020)\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\]

In 2025, Bakare won the [BAFTA TV Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Awards "British Academy Television Awards") for Best Supporting Actor for his performance in _Mr Loverman_.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariyon_Bakare#cite_note-11)

**Varada Sethu** (born **Varada Sethumadhavan**, 12 May 1992) is a British actress. Her credits include _[Sket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sket "Sket")_ (2010), _[English: An Autumn in London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English:_An_Autumn_in_London "English: An Autumn in London")_ (2012), _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctors_/(2000_TV_series/) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_ (2015), _[New Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Blood_/(TV_series/) "New Blood (TV series)")_ (2016), _[Doctor Foster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Foster_/(TV_series/) "Doctor Foster (TV series)")_ (2017), _[Hanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanna_/(TV_series/) "Hanna (TV series)")_ (2019), _[Strike Back: Vendetta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strike_Back:_Vendetta "Strike Back: Vendetta")_ (2020), _[Jurassic World Dominion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic_World_Dominion "Jurassic World Dominion")_ (2022), and _[Annika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annika_/(2021_TV_series/) "Annika (2021 TV series)")_ (2023).

She portrayed [Detective Sergeant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detective_Sergeant "Detective Sergeant") Mishal Ali in _[Hard Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_Sun "Hard Sun")_ (2018), [Cinta Kaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinta_Kaz "Cinta Kaz") in the [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney%2B "Disney+") _[Star Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars "Star Wars")_ series _[Andor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andor_/(TV_series/) "Andor (TV series)")_ (2022–2025), and [Belinda Chandra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra "Belinda Chandra") in _[Doctor Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who "Doctor Who")_ (2025).

Varada Sethumadhavan was born on 12 May 1992 in [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"), India.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-2)[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-dwm-3) She and her twin sister Abhaya are of [Malayali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayali "Malayali") ancestry.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-dwm-3)[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-andor-4) Sethu's parents are doctors. She moved to the North East of England at a young age and she grew up in [Benton, Tyne and Wear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benton,_Tyne_and_Wear "Benton, Tyne and Wear"),[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-chron-5) near [Newcastle upon Tyne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newcastle_upon_Tyne "Newcastle upon Tyne"). Sethu attended [Dame Allan's Schools](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dame_Allan%27s_School,_Newcastle_upon_Tyne "Dame Allan's School, Newcastle upon Tyne") and was a member of the [National Youth Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Youth_Theatre "National Youth Theatre").[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-chron-5) During her final year of [sixth form](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sixth_form "Sixth form"), Sethu won the 2010 Miss Newcastle competition.\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\] She went on to study [veterinary medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veterinary_medicine "Veterinary medicine") at [University of Bristol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Bristol "University of Bristol"), later switching to [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology "Physiology").\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\]

Sethu has been performing the [Indian classical dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_classical_dance "Indian classical dance") traditions of both [Bharatanatyam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatanatyam "Bharatanatyam") and [Mohiniyattam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohiniyattam "Mohiniyattam") from a young age.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-dwm-3) Sethu continued her acting education at the [Identity School of Acting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Identity_School_of_Acting "Identity School of Acting") in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London").[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-mids-6)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-hindu-7)

In 2010, Sethu made her debut appearance on screen in the short film _Impressions_ as Samena.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-imp-8) In 2011, Sethu landed the role of Kiran in the feature film _[Sket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sket "Sket")_,[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-chron-5) then as Meghana Scariah in _[English: An Autumn in London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English:_An_Autumn_in_London "English: An Autumn in London")_ in 2012.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-tv-9) In 2015 she made an appearance as PC Kylie Green in the 2000 TV series _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctors_/(2000_TV_series/) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-tv-9)

Her career continued in 2016 appearing as Peaseblossom in a 2016 TV movie version of _[A Midsummer Night's Dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Midsummer_Night%27s_Dream_/(2016_film/) "A Midsummer Night's Dream (2016 film)")_.,[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-mids-6) _[Now You See Me 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Now_You_See_Me_2 "Now You See Me 2")_ and _[New Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Blood_/(TV_series/) "New Blood (TV series)")_.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-tv-9)

In 2017, Sethu appeared as Aisha in two episodes of _[Doctor Foster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Foster_/(TV_series/) "Doctor Foster (TV series)")_.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-tv-9) In 2018, Sethu starred as DS Mishal Ali for six episodes in the BBC apocalyptic TV crime series _[Hard Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_Sun "Hard Sun")_.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-rad-10)

In 2019, Sethu performed as a series regular in season seven of _[Strike Back: Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strike_Back:_Revolution "Strike Back: Revolution")_ as Lance Corporal Manisha Chetri of the British Army.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-nerd-11)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-strike-12) In 2022, She played rebel Cinta Kaz in both seasons of [_Andor_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andor_/(TV_series/) "Andor (TV series)").[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-andor-4)

In 2025, Sethu portrayed the [companion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Companion_/(Doctor_Who/) "Companion (Doctor Who)") [Belinda Chandra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belinda_Chandra "Belinda Chandra") in _[Doctor Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who "Doctor Who")_ alongside [Ncuti Gatwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa "Ncuti Gatwa") as the [Fifteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor "Fifteenth Doctor") in [series 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15 "Doctor Who series 15").[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-13)[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-RTBC-14) Prior to this, she played Mundy Flynn in the [series 14](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_14 "Doctor Who series 14") episode "[Boom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boom_/(Doctor_Who/) "Boom (Doctor Who)")".[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu#cite_note-15)

Ariyon Bakare is a British actor, writer, and director who has worked across film, television, and theatre since graduating from Drama Centre London. Born and raised in the East End of London, he was brought up by his Nigerian father in the East End. At a young age, Bakare moved to New York City to study dance, However, at twenty-one, he shifted his focus to acting.  
  
Bakare continued his training at the HB Studio in New York, studying under the renowned Uta Hagen, before returning to the UK to attend the prestigious Drama Centre London. There, he studied under theatre luminaries Yat Malgren and Christopher Fettes, two of the UK's most respected acting pedagogues.  
  
In 1998, Bakare made history as the first Black man to lead a BBC period drama, portraying Mehuru in the BAFTA-nominated adaptation of Philippa Gregory's A Respectable Trade. His performance was widely praised for its intelligence and emotional depth.  
  
He gained wider recognition as Dr. Ben Kwarme in the BBC series Doctors (2001-2005), earning nominations for Best Actor at both the Royal Television Society Midlands Awards and the British Soap Awards. His diverse television credits include standout roles in His Dark Materials, Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell, Doctor Who, Carnival Row, Thirteen, Karen Pirie, and Dancing on the Edge.  
  
Bakare's portrayal of Lord Boreal in His Dark Materials garnered a dedicated fan following, further expanding his reach and impact. His recent role as Morris De La Roux in the BBC drama Mr Loverman sparked significant discussion on social media, with audiences praising his nuanced performance and the show's fresh representation of LGBTQ+ narratives within the Black British community. For this role, he won the BAFTA Television Award for Best Supporting Actor in 2025.  
  
His film credits include Life (2017), Rogue One: A Star Wars Story (2016), The Dark Knight (2008), Jupiter Ascending (2015), and After the Rain (1999).  
  
On stage, Bakare has performed with the Royal Shakespeare Company, Royal Court Theatre, and Young Vic. He received an Ian Charleson Award commendation for his role in A Servant to Two Masters, with other notable theatre credits including Julius Caesar, Antony and Cleopatra, The Dream Of The Dog, The Mountaintop, and God of Carnage.  
  
His lead role in the short film "Waiting for Time" earned him multiple Best Actor awards at major international film festivals.  
  
As a writer and director, Bakare has directed episodes of Doctors, co-wrote, and is also the star of the Channel Four drama "Stealing Lives." He was awarded a UK Film Council development grant for his debut feature project, Kodak Cowboy.  
  
He is the founder of the anti-racism initiative iCARE. He serves as an ambassador for WaterAid, delivering a keynote address at St James's Palace in 2025 on global water access and environmental justice. Reflecting on his work, Bakare has said, "I'm not interested in playing stereotypes. I aim to portray human beings as multifaceted and complex.

Doctor Who's Varada Sethu reveals how Belinda is linked to Mundy Flynn
======================================================================

New companion Belinda is "a special person that the Doctor's looking for".

![Image 3](https://media.delight.video/f0cf5e3e9068d9a4affa36d5c8962eaf1a0662ba/cf657a7011ea762c285715cd9ea62a176f81c40d/POSTER_USER/v0/743748fa-843f-41dc-8253-55c671c22dec.jpg?quality=90)

Varada Sethu is set to return to Doctor Who – but not as her former character Mundy Flynn, with the [Andor](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/andor-season-2-disney-plus-release-date/) star instead playing a new character, Belinda Chandra, in the BBC sci-fi's latest episodes.

Ad

The show won't simply ignore the fact that these two characters are portrayed by the same actor, however – instead, the link between Mundy (who appeared in last year's [Boom](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-boom/)) and Belinda will be addressed in the new season, and will be part of a story arc involving Sethu's companion.

Speaking to [RadioTimes.com](https://www.radiotimes.com/) at the launch of the new season, Sethu confirmed that there is a "genetic link" between the pair.

"It spans, obviously, thousands of years – and it's like an added layer of why she's a special person that the Doctor's looking for," she teased.

Belinda's connection to Mundy will be "acknowledged straight away", added [Doctor Who](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-season-15-release-date/) showrunner Russell T Davies, who also pointed to past instances of Doctor Who bringing back previous guest stars to play companion characters.

![Image 6: Varada Sethu as Belinda Chandra in Doctor Who holding a pack](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/04/516626-e56e56e.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Varada Sethu as Belinda Chandra in Doctor Who. BBC

"There's a fine old tradition of this. We did that with Freema \[Agyeman, who played Martha Jones\], where she played her own cousin who was murdered by the Cybermen. Brilliant! How did we think of that? Amazing!

"That's been going on forever... Ian Marter, who played Harry in the Tom Baker era, he'd appeared in a story called [Carnival of Monsters](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-guide/carnival-of-monsters/). Peter Purves did that way back in 1966, \[playing the one-off character Morton Dill, before returning as [companion Steven Taylor](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-peter-purves-exit-newsupdate/)\].

"So it's all been done before, but this time the Doctor clearly thinks, 'Oh, I've seen someone that looks like you before' – he clearly says out loud, 'Is this a coincidence?' – keep watching!"

![Image 7: Belinda and the Doctor standing next to the TARDIS and looking open-mouthed with excitement. Belinda is holding the Doctor's arm.](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/03/doctor-who-varada-sethu-ncuti-gatwa-5d215cd.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Varada Sethu as Belinda Chandra and Ncuti Gatwa as the Doctor in Doctor Who. BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/Lara Cornell

Sethu has described Belinda as "[the main character of her own story](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/varada-sethu-doctor-who/)" who is not "in awe" of the Doctor – and fans can also look forward to [the return of Millie Gibson as Ruby Sunday](https://www.radiotimes.com/app/millie-gibson-addresses-how-much-fans-can-expect-to-see-ruby-in-new-season-of-doctor-who/).

Additionally, Anita Dobson is set to reprise her role as the enigmatic Mrs Flood, [hinting at intriguing developments for her character](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-anita-dobson-mrs-flood-mindset-newsupdate/). ​

Other guest stars include [Freddie Fox](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-freddie-fox-newsupdate/), [Christopher Chung](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-season-15-christopher-chung-first-look-newsupdate/), [Rose Ayling-Ellis](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-casts-rose-ayling-ellis-season-15-newsupdate/), and returning faces from UNIT, such as Jemma Redgrave and Bonnie Langford.
