From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
The Doctor
The Fifteenth Doctor
Doctor Who character

Ncuti Gatwa as the Fifteenth Doctor

First regular appearance"The Church on Ruby Road" (2023)
Last regular appearance"The Reality War" (2025)
Introduced byRussell T Davies
Portrayed byNcuti Gatwa
Preceded byDavid Tennant (Fourteenth Doctor)
Information
Tenure25 December 2023 – 31 May 2025
No of series2
Appearances16 stories (18 episodes)
Companions
  • Ruby Sunday
  • Joy Almondo
  • Belinda Chandra
Chronology
  • Specials (2023)
  • Series 14 (2024)
  • Series 15 (2025)
The **Fifteenth Doctor** is an incarnation of [the Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Doctor "The Doctor"), the [protagonist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protagonist "Protagonist") of the British [science fiction television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_fiction_television "Science fiction television") series _[Doctor Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who "Doctor Who")_. He is portrayed by Rwandan-Scottish actor [Ncuti Gatwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ncuti_Gatwa "Ncuti Gatwa") in two series and two specials.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-BBC_News_Gatwa-1) As with previous incarnations of the Doctor, the character has also appeared in [_Doctor Who_ spin-offs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_spin-offs "Doctor Who spin-offs"), both during and after the character's televised appearances. Within the series' narrative, the Doctor is a millennia-old [alien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extraterrestrial_life "Extraterrestrial life") [Time Lord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Lord "Time Lord") from the planet [Gallifrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallifrey "Gallifrey"), with somewhat unknown origins, who [travels in time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_travel "Time travel") and space in their [TARDIS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TARDIS "TARDIS"), frequently with companions. Usually, at the end of each incarnation's life, the Doctor [regenerates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regeneration_/(Doctor_Who/) "Regeneration (Doctor Who)"); as a result, their physical appearance and personality changes. However, the Fifteenth Doctor emerged unconventionally, via "bi-generation", in which he split from his predecessor, the [Fourteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourteenth_Doctor "Fourteenth Doctor")'s body, rather than replacing him, allowing both incarnations to co-exist. In contrast to his predecessors, Gatwa portrays a Doctor who is attempting to let go of much of his recent emotional trauma, with a more emotionally balanced, liberated, fun-loving, and affectionate outward persona. In contrast to previous Doctors, the Fifteenth Doctor's stories include a greater focus on fantasy elements, intended by showrunner Russell T Davies to "increase the danger" and have a "bigger, wider sense of imagination".[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-2) His first episode as lead actor aired on 25 December 2023,[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-3) and his [first full series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_14 "Doctor Who series 14") premiered on 11 May 2024.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-DCHTCAK-4) The Fifteenth Doctor regenerated in the series 15 finale, "[The Reality War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War "The Reality War")", into a character played by [Billie Piper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Piper "Billie Piper"). [![Image 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/45/Ncuti_Gatwa-65777.jpg/250px-Ncuti_Gatwa-65777.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ncuti_Gatwa-65777.jpg) Ncuti Gatwa (pictured in 2024) portrays the Fifteenth Doctor Before Gatwa's casting was announced, several actors were heavily rumoured to be taking over from Whittaker, including [Hugh Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugh_Grant "Hugh Grant"), [Michael Sheen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Sheen "Michael Sheen"), [Kris Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Marshall "Kris Marshall"), [Richard Ayoade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Ayoade "Richard Ayoade"), [Michaela Coel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Coel "Michaela Coel"), [Kelly Macdonald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Macdonald "Kelly Macdonald"), and [Lenny Henry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenny_Henry "Lenny Henry"). Russell T Davies' return as the programme's showrunner also led to speculation that an actor he had previously worked with in other projects would join him as the [Fourteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourteenth_Doctor "Fourteenth Doctor"), with [Olly Alexander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olly_Alexander "Olly Alexander"), [Lydia West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lydia_West "Lydia West"), [Omari Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omari_Douglas "Omari Douglas"), [T'Nia Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T%27Nia_Miller "T'Nia Miller"), and [Fisayo Akinade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisayo_Akinade "Fisayo Akinade") ranking highly in bookies' odds.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-5) Rumours also circulated that [David Tennant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Tennant "David Tennant") would reprise his role, having previously portrayed the [Tenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenth_Doctor "Tenth Doctor") during executive producer [Russell T Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell_T_Davies "Russell T Davies")'s initial time as showrunner, or that [Jo Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin "Jo Martin"), who debuted as the [Fugitive Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor "Fugitive Doctor") during Whittaker's tenure, would be revealed as the Fourteenth incarnation.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-6) On 8 May 2022, Gatwa posted an Instagram picture featuring two red heart emojis, a plus sign, and a blue box emoji.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-7) The post, alongside comments from incoming _Doctor Who_ showrunner Russell T Davies,[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-8) led to speculation that Gatwa had been cast as the Doctor. This was later confirmed that same day by the official _Doctor Who_ Twitter account.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-Ncuti_announcement-9) Gatwa is the first black actor,[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-10) first African-born actor, and first openly [queer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queer "Queer") actor to headline as the Doctor.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-12) He is also the fourth Scottish actor to play the character.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-13)[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-14) In an article released on the _Doctor Who_ website, Gatwa said, "This role and show means so much to so many around the world, including myself, and each one of my incredibly talented predecessors has handled that unique responsibility and privilege with the utmost care. I will endeavour my utmost to do the same."[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-Ncuti_announcement-9) Davies added, "Ncuti dazzled us, seized hold of the Doctor and owned those TARDIS keys in seconds... I promise you, 2023 will be spectacular!"[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-Ncuti_announcement-9) Gatwa had previously been announced as [Jodie Whittaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Whittaker "Jodie Whittaker")'s successor as the programme's lead, and many reports stated he would play the Fourteenth Doctor and that Whittaker's [Thirteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteenth_Doctor "Thirteenth Doctor") would regenerate into Gatwa's incarnation.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-BBC_News_Gatwa-1)[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-15) At the conclusion of Whittaker's final episode, "[The Power of the Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Power_of_the_Doctor "The Power of the Doctor")" (2022), her Doctor instead regenerated into a form similar to the [Tenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenth_Doctor "Tenth Doctor"). Gatwa was subsequently confirmed as the Fifteenth Doctor, following Tennant's [Fourteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourteenth_Doctor "Fourteenth Doctor")'s tenure over the [2023 specials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_specials_/(2023/) "Doctor Who specials (2023)"). Davies stated "the path to Ncuti's 15th Doctor is laden with mystery, horror, robots, puppets, danger and fun!"[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-DCHTCAK-4) Gatwa appeared in character for the first time in the trailer for the 2023 specials.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-16) > I came to the show with that notion, thinking, 'Why do we keep repeating the same clothes?' To be blunt, with the bigger budget, we have the freedom to play and explore this stuff. Russell T Davies[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-17) In a departure for the character of the Doctor, the Fifteenth Doctor wears a variety of clothing rather than adopting one distinct style.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-18) Pam Downe, a costume designer who had previously worked on the [60th anniversary specials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_specials_/(2023/) "Doctor Who specials (2023)"), was tasked with designing the Doctor's extensive wardrobe. Downe first drew up numerous [mood boards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mood_board "Mood board") containing different ideas for the costumes, and presented them to Gatwa and the production team; the boards included "all kinds of gender-pushing, societal-pushing outfits".[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-EWCover-19) One of them was an image of a "well-known [American football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football") player" wearing a "suit skirt"; though Downe thought they would have to "wait a bit of time" before introducing that, as it's "such a big jump from former Doctors."[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-20) Gatwa likened the Doctor to [Captain Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_Britain "Captain Britain"), and wanted "to travel through all the subcultures of Britain" through the Doctor's fashion.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-EWCover-19) Davies said he was familiar with [cosplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosplay "Cosplay") and wanted cosplayers to have "a great big swimming pool" of costumes to replicate. He also wanted to "put it back into the children's house", with clothes that every child has "under the stairs somewhere."[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-21) Gatwa's initial inclination for the Fifteenth Doctor's style was inspired by [Ralph Lauren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Lauren "Ralph Lauren")'s "preppy" designs in collaboration with [Morehouse College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morehouse_College "Morehouse College") and [Spelman College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spelman_College "Spelman College"), noting the colleges' Black histories. The production team opted for less "traditional" looks, wanting to "push it forward".[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-Vogue-22) Interviewer Devan Coggan disclosed that the Fifteenth Doctor's costumes were designed to reflect the planet or time period visited in each episode, including a [Regency era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regency_era "Regency era") costume for the episode "[Rogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogue_/(Doctor_Who/) "Rogue (Doctor Who)")" and a "meticulously tailored pinstripe suit" for the 1960s-set "[The Devil's Chord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Devil%27s_Chord "The Devil's Chord")".[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-EWCover-19) The Doctor's suit was inspired by images of [the Rolling Stones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rolling_Stones "The Rolling Stones").[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-QuinnStyle-23) In the 2023 Christmas special "[The Church on Ruby Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Church_on_Ruby_Road "The Church on Ruby Road")", the Doctor wears three different costumes; including a [kilt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilt "Kilt") and [vest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waistcoat "Waistcoat") when dancing in a [nightclub](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nightclub "Nightclub"). Downe said this was a "chance to see how far we could go and it works because he can really wear it."[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-QuinnStyle-23) The leather coat worn by the Doctor in both the special and first episode "[Space Babies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Babies "Space Babies")" was inspired by "seventies America" mixed with "UK-based eighties [ska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ska "Ska")", with the trousers inspired by [Gurkha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gurkha "Gurkha") trousers.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-QuinnStyle-23) The photoshoot for Coggan's interview also revealed two costumes from [series 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15 "Doctor Who series 15"), described as "an elaborate tartan jacket with a kilt and a stunning all-white look".[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-EWCover-19) Downe also incorporated references to previous Doctors in Gatwa's costumes; Louise Griffin of _[Radio Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Times "Radio Times")_ noted that Gatwa's costume for "Rogue" includes a maroon [velvet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Velvet "Velvet") [tailcoat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tailcoat "Tailcoat") reminiscent of the [Third Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Doctor "Third Doctor")'s ([Jon Pertwee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Pertwee "Jon Pertwee")) [smoking jackets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoking_jacket "Smoking jacket") and [blazers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blazer "Blazer").[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-24) Gatwa expressed an affinity for the style of Pertwee's Doctor, jokingly claiming that "our Doctors are the only two who dress like sluts".[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-25) Writing in _[British Vogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Vogue "British Vogue")_, Radhika Seth described the Fifteenth Doctor's early costumes as ranging "from a tangerine-coloured knit and a bright blue double-breasted [pinstripe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinstripe "Pinstripe") suit, to a glossy leather [trenchcoat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trenchcoat "Trenchcoat") paired with a [cardigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardigan_/(sweater/) "Cardigan (sweater)") zipped down to expose his chest and a set of delicate gold necklaces, summarising that "_Doctor Who_ is getting sexy".[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-Vogue-22) Prior to the first appearance of the Fifteenth Doctor, Gatwa made an uncredited cameo as himself, in costume as the Doctor, during an edited repeat of the 2013 docudrama _[An Adventure in Space and Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An_Adventure_in_Space_and_Time "An Adventure in Space and Time")_, airing on 23 November 2023, _Doctor Who_'s sixtieth anniversary. In the original version, while preparing to film his [regeneration scene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tenth_Planet "The Tenth Planet"), [William Hartnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Hartnell "William Hartnell") ([David Bradley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Bradley_/(English_actor/) "David Bradley (English actor)")) looks across the TARDIS console and sees a vision of [Matt Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Smith "Matt Smith"), the actor who played the then-incumbent [Eleventh Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eleventh_Doctor "Eleventh Doctor") during the show's fiftieth anniversary year. For the 2023 repeat, the scene was edited to replace Smith with Gatwa.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-26) Gatwa first appears as the Fifteenth Doctor in the 60th anniversary special episode "[The Giggle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Giggle "The Giggle")", appearing in the final third of the story as the [Fourteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourteenth_Doctor "Fourteenth Doctor") ([David Tennant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Tennant "David Tennant")) appears to regenerate but instead "bi-generates", introducing the new Doctor as a separate physical entity. The two Doctors team up to defeat the malevolent deity the Toymaker ([Neil Patrick Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Patrick_Harris "Neil Patrick Harris")), and later use the remaining power of the latter's lingering reality-warping domain to duplicate the TARDIS. The Fifteenth Doctor shares some words of wisdom with his predecessor, who returns the favour by wishing him luck, before setting off for new adventures in his version of the TARDIS. The Doctor next appears in "[The Church on Ruby Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Church_on_Ruby_Road "The Church on Ruby Road")" in which he meets new companion [Ruby Sunday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruby_Sunday "Ruby Sunday") ([Millie Gibson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millie_Gibson "Millie Gibson")) and faces off against [goblins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goblin "Goblin"). In the subsequent episodes, the Doctor and Ruby encounter a surprising amount of magical and supernatural threats, including a [fairy circle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairy_circle "Fairy circle") in "[73 Yards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/73_Yards "73 Yards")" and Maestro ([Jinkx Monsoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jinkx_Monsoon "Jinkx Monsoon")), the child of the Toymaker, in "[The Devil's Chord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Devil%27s_Chord "The Devil's Chord")". Maestro warns that more evil extra-dimensional gods from their pantheon are pursuing the Doctor, including "The One Who Waits". Ruby herself also exhibits strange qualities when her life is endangered, frequently conjuring the heavy snow from the day she was abandoned at the church of Ruby Road as baby. Late in the season, the Doctor begins a romance with a time and space travelling male bounty hunter known as Rogue ([Jonathan Groff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Groff "Jonathan Groff")) in the episode [of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogue_/(Doctor_Who/) "Rogue (Doctor Who)").[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-27) Over the course of the season, the Doctor and Ruby repeatedly encounter the same woman's likeness (played by [Susan Twist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Twist "Susan Twist")) across time and space, which they first begin to notice in "[Dot and Bubble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dot_and_Bubble "Dot and Bubble")". In "[The Legend of Ruby Sunday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Legend_of_Ruby_Sunday "The Legend of Ruby Sunday")", the Doctor attempts to solve the mystery of Ruby's origins and the mysterious woman. They uncover that "The One Who Waits" is the Doctor's old enemy Sutekh ([Gabriel Woolf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabriel_Woolf "Gabriel Woolf")), the god of death, and that he has been secretly attached to the Doctor's TARDIS for most of his travels. In the end, the Doctor and Ruby defeat Sutekh, and say a bittersweet goodbye in "[Empire of Death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_of_Death_/(Doctor_Who_episode/) "Empire of Death (Doctor Who episode)")" after reuniting Ruby with her birth mother. In "[Joy to the World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joy_to_the_World_/(Doctor_Who/) "Joy to the World (Doctor Who)")", the Doctor meets one-off companion Joy ([Nicola Coughlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicola_Coughlan "Nicola Coughlan")), but also spends a year working in a small hotel to complete a closed loop that will allow him to obtain a key passcode, befriending the hotel manager Anita (Steph de Whalley). In [series 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15 "Doctor Who series 15"), the Doctor is joined by a new companion, Belinda Chandra ([Varada Sethu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varada_Sethu "Varada Sethu")).[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-BelindaJoy-28) The series follows the Doctor as he attempts to return Belinda to Earth on 24 May 2025. Because the TARDIS cannot land there, he invents a device called the vindicator to create a web of locations across time and space to help him get there. Along the way, the Doctor faxes off with another member of the Pantheon in the form of the god of light, Lux Imperator ([Alan Cumming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Cumming "Alan Cumming")) in "[Lux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lux_/(Doctor_Who/) "Lux (Doctor Who)")", as well as a former acolyte of various gods of stories in “[The Story & the Engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Story_%26_the_Engine "The Story & the Engine")”. On their final stop, in "[The Interstellar Song Contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Interstellar_Song_Contest "The Interstellar Song Contest")", the pair learn Earth was destroyed on 24 May 2025. In “[Wish World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wish_World "Wish World")”, it is revealed the Doctor’s nemesis [the Rani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rani_/(Doctor_Who/) "Rani (Doctor Who)") ([Archie Panjabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Panjabi "Archie Panjabi")) magnified the powers of the god of wishes, Desiderum, to replace Earth with a fantasy reality that would fracture under its internal contradictions to facilitate the release of the Time Lord founder [Omega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omega_/(Doctor_Who/) "Omega (Doctor Who)") on 24 May 2025. After Rani and Omega’s defeat in “[The Reality War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War "The Reality War")”, the Doctor feels forced to trigger his regeneration in order to subtly [alter reality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retcon "Retcon") and bring back Poppy, who had been his daughter with Belinda in the Rani’s fantasy world. Thanks to some timely advice from his [thirteenth incarnation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteenth_Doctor "Thirteenth Doctor") ([Jodie Whittaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Whittaker "Jodie Whittaker")), Poppy returns – but now fully human, and no longer the Doctor’s child. Leaving Belinda and Poppy behind, he returns to the TARDIS and completes his regeneration, assuming a familiar face ([Billie Piper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billie_Piper "Billie Piper")). [Daleks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalek "Dalek"), and stated he would be "angry" if not given the chance.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-30) Nevertheless, at the close "[The Reality War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Reality_War "The Reality War")", Gatwa's Fifteenth Doctor underwent a surprise credits.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-32) While Gatwa insisted it was "always the plan" for him to only spend a short time playing the lead role because of its At the 2022 Paris Fan Festival, [Matt Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Smith "Matt Smith"), who portrayed the [Eleventh Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eleventh_Doctor "Eleventh Doctor"), openly expressed his support to Gatwa taking on the role.[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-43) In an interview with [STV News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STV_News "STV News"), [Peter Capaldi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Capaldi "Peter Capaldi"), who portrayed the [Twelfth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twelfth_Doctor "Twelfth Doctor"), stated that he believed that Gatwa would be "an amazing Doctor." During the [2022 British Academy Television Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_British_Academy_Television_Awards "2022 British Academy Television Awards"), Gatwa stated that [David Tennant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Tennant "David Tennant"), who portrayed the [Tenth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenth_Doctor "Tenth Doctor") and [Fourteenth Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourteenth_Doctor "Fourteenth Doctor"), and Jodie Whittaker, who played the [Thirteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteenth_Doctor "Thirteenth Doctor"), both called him to express their support.[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-44) Following the broadcast of "[The Church on Ruby Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Church_on_Ruby_Road "The Church on Ruby Road")", Martin Belam of _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")_ said Gatwa "totally owned the episode".[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-45) Jordan King of _[Empire Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_Magazine "Empire Magazine")_ described his performance as "a breath of fresh air" and said he was "a real gift".[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-46) Gatwa's performance in Series 14 earned praise from critics. Many writers for _[The Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Independent "The Independent")_ called Gatwa's acting "interstellar" and "mesmerising".[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-47)[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-48) Naina Bajekal of [_Time_ magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_/(magazine/) "Time (magazine)") believed that Gatwa was "bringing _Doctor Who_ into a new era".[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-49) [Mary McNamara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_McNamara "Mary McNamara") of _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ called Gatwa "an absolute delight" and wrote that his "unbridled exuberance makes this an easy sell and serves as a data bridge between new viewers and old."[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-50) Conversely, some reviewers were critical of the writing for the Fifteenth Doctor and his tenure, Gatwa's casting, or both. During Series 14, Craig Elvy of _Screen Rant_ wrote the Doctor "keeps treading on trouble, running away, and relying more on luck than judgment to save the day."[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-51) Reviewing "[Joy to the World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joy_to_the_World_/(Doctor_Who/) "Joy to the World (Doctor Who)")", Martin Robinson felt the Doctor had failed to find his footing. He thought his multiple instances of crying "started to come across as meaningless", citing the character as lacking warmth in various scenes.[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-52) Following his departure, _[The Daily Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Daily_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")_'s Michael Hogan felt that Gatwa's Doctor had "flopped", in part due to his lack of gravitas and "mainstream recognisability", poor scripts, and Gatwa's apparent lack of devotion to the role.[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-53) Sarah Carson of _[i News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Independent "The Independent")_ similarly felt Gatwa's casting was overambitious for "an ascendant star, in huge demand, with limitless potential".[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-54) Robert Anderson from _[IGN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IGN "IGN")_ thought that Gatwa had enormous potential for _Doctor Who_, possessing "flashes of brilliance", but criticised the shorter seasons, the writing, and the handling of Gatwa's exit, feeling the actor had been "short-changed".[\[55\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_note-IGN-55) 1. ^ [_**a**_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_ref-BBC_News_Gatwa_1-0) [_**b**_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor#cite_ref-BBC_News_Gatwa_1-1) ["Ncuti Gatwa: BBC names actor as next Doctor Who star"](https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-61371123). Published: 08:00 pm, 31 May 2025

     ![Image 1: The Doctor fires regeneration energy at the TARDIS console](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/images/ic/400xn/p0lfp7dp.jpg)

(Image: BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon)

In Doctor Who season 2 finale The Reality War viewers saw Ncuti Gatwa’s final scenes as the Doctor as he steps down from one of the most iconic roles in British television.

In an epic two-part season finale, viewers saw the Doctor face the Rani in an extraordinary battle to save the world and the Doctor made the ultimate sacrifice to save the life of one little girl.

*   **[Watch Doctor Who on BBC iPlayer and add to your Watchlist](https://www.bbc.co.uk/iplayer/episodes/p0gglvqn/doctor-who)**

     ![Image 2: The Doctor reaches towards the ceiling while regeneration energy streams from their hands](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/images/ic/400xn/p0lfp7xc.jpg)

(Image: BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon)

Since being announced as the Doctor in May 2022, Ncuti Gatwa was launched into the Whoniverse and immediately taken into the hearts of Doctor Who fans across the globe. With his first appearance being part of the show’s 60th anniversary celebrations in November 2023, Gatwa’s arrival into the show was a never seen before bi-generation which saw him split from the Fourteenth Doctor, played by David Tennant.

His portrayal of the Doctor won Gatwa a Best Actor award at the BAFTA Cymru Awards in 2024, as well as nominations for a BAFTA Scotland Audience Award for Favourite Scot on Screen, and Best Actor in a Drama Series at The Critics Choice Television Awards in the US in 2025.

     ![Image 3: Nucti Gatwa as The Doctor, standing outside on a dark night in snow, with glittering lights in the background](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/images/ic/400xn/p0gwwmlk.jpg)

(Image: BBC Studios)

Gatwa’s first full episode, The Church on Ruby Road saw the Doctor team up with companion Ruby Sunday, played by Millie Gibson, and the two travelled on out of this world adventures, with episodes including The Devil’s Chord, Rogue and Boom with Gatwa winning praise globally for his iteration of the iconic character.

In season two, Gatwa gained another companion, Belinda Chandra, played by Varada Sethu and the stakes got higher, with battles bigger than ever before with the duo going back in time to Miami in Lux, travelling to Lagos in The Story & the Engine as well as attending the 803rd Interstellar Song Contest before facing the Rani and Omega in his final battle to save earth before regenerating once more.

     ![Image 4: The Thirteenth Doctor (Jodie Whittaker) and Fifteenth Doctor (Ncuti Gatwa) stand face to face at the TARDIS console](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/images/ic/400xn/p0lfp864.jpg)

(Image: BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon)

Speaking of his decision to leave, Ncuti said: “You know when you get cast, at some point you are going to have to hand back that sonic screwdriver and it is all going to come to an end, but nothing quite prepares you for it. This journey has been one that I will never forget, and a role that will be part of me forever. There are no words to describe what it feels like to be cast as the Doctor, nor are there words to explain what it feels like to be accepted into this iconic role that has existed for over 60 years and is truly loved by so many across the globe.

"The fans are truly the final character and beating heart of this show and I can’t thank the Whoniverse, and the Whovians, enough for welcoming me in, and making this such a touching experience. I’ve loved every minute of it, but now is the time to hand over the keys to that beloved blue box and let someone else take control and enjoy it every bit as much as I have. I’ll truly miss it, and forever be grateful to it, and everyone that has played a part in my journey as the Doctor.”

     ![Image 5: The Doctor stands on the TARDIS, smiling](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/images/ic/400xn/p0lfp8mf.jpg)

(Image: BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon)

Speaking of Ncuti’s departure, Russell T Davies, Showrunner said: "What a Doctor! Thank you, Ncuti! As his final words say, this has been an absolute joy, and the team in Cardiff and everyone who has worked on this show for the past few years, are so lucky to have been part of Ncuti’s great adventure as he shoots off to stratospheric new heights."

     ![Image 6: The Doctor stands at the door of the TARDIS in space, regenerating](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/images/ic/400xn/p0lfp804.jpg)

(Image: BBC Studios/Bad Wolf)

Lindsay Salt, Director of Drama added: “When Ncuti Gatwa first stepped foot on the TARDIS we instantly knew he was going to be an iconic Doctor and it wasn’t long before his dazzling performances captured the hearts of so many around the globe. The role of the Doctor is like no other and Ncuti’s dedication, charisma and magnetism has taken the Doctor into unchartered territory which we have never experienced before. As Ncuti himself said at the start of this journey - unlike the Doctor he may only have one heart, but he is giving it all to this role - I think we can all agree that he did that, and more. Thanks, Ncuti for being such a special part of the Whoniverse.”

### **But as viewers said goodbye to the Fifteenth Doctor they got a hello from a much-loved face...**

     ![Image 7: A woman with blonde hair smiles as her face emerges through regeneration energy](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/images/ic/400xn/p0lfp8mw.jpg)

As everyone said farewell to this iconic Doctor, they also got sight of a very familiar face as the Doctor regenerated and it was none other than Billie Piper...

Billie first appeared in the Whoniverse when Doctor Who returned to screens in 2005, as Rose Tyler, the much-loved Companion to the Doctor played by Christopher Eccleston and David Tennant. But just how and why she is back remains to be seen…

Speaking of the surprise twist, Russell T Davies adds: "Billie once changed the whole of television, back in 2005, and now she’s done it again! It’s an honour and a hoot to welcome her back to the TARDIS, but quite how and why and who is a story yet to be told. After 62 years, the Doctor’s adventures are only just beginning!"

Speaking of her return, Billie says: "It’s no secret how much I love this show, and I have always said I would love to return to the Whoniverse as I have some of my best memories there, so to be given the opportunity to step back on that TARDIS one more time was just something I couldn’t refuse, but who, how, why and when, you’ll just have to wait and see."

Doctor Who is produced by Bad Wolf with BBC Studios for the BBC and Disney Branded Television.

**Jo Martin** (born 29 April[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin#cite_note-2) 1969[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin#cite_note-3)[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin#cite_note-4)) is a British actress. On television, she is known for her roles in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") series _[The Crouches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Crouches "The Crouches")_ (2003–2005) as Natalie Crouch,[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin#cite_note-5) _[Back to Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back_to_Life_/(TV_series/) "Back to Life (TV series)")_ (2019–2021) as Janice, _[Holby City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holby_City "Holby City")_ (2019–2022) as [Max McGerry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_McGerry "Max McGerry"),[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin#cite_note-6) and _[Doctor Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who "Doctor Who")_ (2020–2022, 2025) as the [Fugitive Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor "Fugitive Doctor"),[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin#cite_note-7) _[Dreaming Whilst Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreaming_Whilst_Black "Dreaming Whilst Black")_ (2023) as Grace and _[The Marlow Murder Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Marlow_Murder_Club_/(TV_series/) "The Marlow Murder Club (TV series)")_ (2024–present) as Suzy Harris.

Martin was born on 29 April 1969 in [Newham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newham "Newham"), London to Jamaican parents. Her mother died on [Christmas Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_Day "Christmas Day") 2015.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin#cite_note-8) Her parents arrived in the area in the 1950s. She attended Portway Primary School and Plashet All Girls Secondary School.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin#cite_note-9)

Martin first appeared in the [series 12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_/(series_12/) "Doctor Who (series 12)") episode "[Fugitive of the Judoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_of_the_Judoon "Fugitive of the Judoon")", playing Ruth Clayton, a tourist guide who is later revealed to be an unplaced incarnation of [the Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Doctor_/(Doctor_Who/) "The Doctor (Doctor Who)") known as the [Fugitive Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor "Fugitive Doctor"). Martin's Doctor received positive reviews from critics.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin#cite_note-10)[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin#cite_note-11) She reprised her role in the series finale, "[The Timeless Children](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Timeless_Children "The Timeless Children")",[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin#cite_note-12) in the third chapter of _[Doctor Who: Flux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who:_Flux "Doctor Who: Flux")_, "[Once, Upon Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Once,_Upon_Time "Once, Upon Time")",[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin#cite_note-13) and in the [2022 special](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_/(2022_specials/) "Doctor Who (2022 specials)") "[The Power of the Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Power_of_the_Doctor "The Power of the Doctor")". Martin later returned to the role in a cameo appearance in the 2025 episode "[The Story & the Engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Story_%26_the_Engine "The Story & the Engine")".

Martin stars in _The Fugitive Doctor Adventures_, an audio drama series focused on her character produced by [Big Finish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Finish_Productions "Big Finish Productions").[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin#cite_note-14)

### _Tales from the Front Line_

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jo_Martin&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Tales from the Front Line")\]

In November 2020, [Talawa Theatre Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talawa_Theatre_Company "Talawa Theatre Company") released _Tales from the Front Line_.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin#cite_note-auto-15)[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin#cite_note-16) The first film presented a verbatim narrative from a teacher, played by Martin, talking about trying to keep themselves and their pupils safe during the pandemic,\[_[specify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing_sources "Wikipedia:Citing sources")_\] the emotional and psychological impact of the global [Black Lives Matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Lives_Matter "Black Lives Matter") movement, and the challenges of supporting students' education during an era of great uncertainty.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin#cite_note-17)

Reviews described Martin's performance as "performed so subtly" as to seem real, while being "conversational and natural".[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin#cite_note-18)[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin#cite_note-19)[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin#cite_note-20)[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin#cite_note-21)

31.content:
Anansi
------

**Author:** Traditional

**Time Period:** 1001 CE–1500 CE

**Country or Culture:** Caribbean

**Genre:** Folktale

Overview
--------

West African tales of a trickster spider came to the New World along with slavery. This spider was a liminal figure whose dwelling in the rafters of homes symbolized his suspension between earth and heaven. He was also a shape-shifter, appearing sometimes as a man or a woman and sometimes as a god. Even the spelling of his name changes throughout the tales: Ananse, Anansi, Aunt Nancy, Anancy, Hanansi, and Annancy.

This character became a means of subversive [storytelling](https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/education/storytelling): slaves could relate Anansi’s adventures, correlating them to their own lives and the ways in which they subverted the plantation order and triumphed over dull-witted masters. Ironically, many slave owners asked to hear these stories told, not realizing their import. Anansi’s primary goal is the fulfilling of his own desires—for food, power, stories, or sex. To do so, he tricks other animals or eats his own children.

Like their protagonist, the tales shift in shape and emphasis, bearing more or less resemblance to other [trickster tales](https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/literature-and-writing/trickster-tale) found in African cultures, particularly among the Akan people. Folklorist Martha Warren Beckwith gathered _Jamaica Anansi Stories_, the collection of tales being examined here, during the 1920s in Jamaica. She had studied with the eminent ethnographer Franz Boas, who had encouraged Zora Neale Hurston’s groundbreaking work among Afro-Caribbean people and who edited Beckwith’s collection. Beckwith also included musical notation, riddles, and cross-references to tales from other cultures.

Beckwith took the unusual step of recording the stories in the Jamaican dialect, regarding the language worth saving as a testimony to the spirit of those who survived the Middle Passage and slavery in the Caribbean. She also gave the names of more than sixty storytellers and the locations where the stories were recorded. The tales were gathered during two trips to Jamaica in 1919 and 1921.

Anansi and his wife and children are major characters in the tales. (Tacoomah is sometimes the name of his wife, and in other tales, Tacoomah is Anansi’s son or neighbor.) Other animals appear as well: Tiger is Anansi’s natural enemy, and sheep are stolen and consumed. Various human characters, generally to be outwitted, also feature in the stories.

To study these tales, postcolonial theory is most appropriate. [Postcolonial theory](https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/political-science/postcolonial-theory) looks at the effects of Western colonialism and its aftermath, culturally and ideologically. Considered by most scholars to have begun with the 1952 publication of Martinique-born Frantz Fanon’s _Black Skin, White Masks_, the theory studies the effect of [colonialism](https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/anthropology/colonialism) on native peoples. Fanon, who was both a psychiatrist and a revolutionary, was interested in the language of Western colonizers and how it caused native peoples to internalize a sense of inferiority and a tendency to suppress their original culture.

According to Fanon, three distinct phases exist in colonialism. First, the colonized people assimilate the cultural model. Next, there is an internal examining of the response and a search for more authentic national roots. Finally, there is a choice for liberation, through violence if need be. Fanon himself worked for the Algerian National Liberation Front from 1957 to 1961. Although Fanon was focusing on the struggles for independence in Algeria, India, and the Middle East, his ideas have been applied to other areas, including the Caribbean.

Summary
-------

The majority of tales collected by Beckwith feature the cunning trickster Anansi, his family, and his enemies. Some of the tales are variants of others within the collection. A few include morals or explanations of natural phenomenon, such as why Anansi lives in the rafters of a house. Anansi is a shape-shifter as well as a trickster. Defining Anansi’s form is therefore a seemingly impossible task. he is sometimes a woman (Aunt Nancy), sometimes a man, and sometimes a spider. He is noted for his cleverness, although he does not always succeed in his aims. In a few of the stories, he dies.

> “He \[Anansi\] saw a man giving a woman some money and telling her to put it up for ‘rainy day.’ After the man had left, Anansi went up to the woman and told her he was ‘Mr. Rainy Day.’ She said, ‘Well, it’s you, sah? My husband been putting up money for you for ten years now. He has quite a bag of it, and I’m so afraid of robbers I’m glad you come!’ So Anansi took the money and returned home and lived contentedly for the rest of his days.”

“Anansi Seeks His Fortune”

Anansi’s overriding concern is to have his own needs met and does not make an effort to provide for his family’s needs. Sometimes he eats all of the food or hides it, leaving his wife (named Tacoomah or Aso) and children (of varying numbers and names) hungry. Several tales highlight his use of cunning to obtain food. For example, in two versions of tale 11, “Throwing Away Knives,” Anansi tells Tiger to toss away his knife, claiming to do the same. When they arrive at a pineapple field, however, Anansi still has his knife but refuses to share it with Tiger, and thus he alone can eat the pineapples. In the second tale, the other character is a sheep with a spoon. Anansi tricks the sheep into leaving his spoon behind. Anansi then eats all the food before the sheep returns from retrieving the spoon.

Some of the tales also explain why animals act a certain way, similar to the _[Just So Stories](https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/literature-and-writing/just-so-stories-rudyard-kipling)_ of Rudyard Kipling. Tale 18, “Goat on the Hill-side,” for example, offers an explanation as to why goats remain on hilly ground: during a time of hunger, Anansi and Tacoomah use the ruse of Tacoomah being ill to lure other animals to the house, one by one. Then they kill each animal and put it in a barrel to be preserved. Goat notices that many animals go into the small house but do not emerge. When Goat goes near the house to investigate, Tacoomah invites him in, but he runs back up the hillside, his now-preferred place.

Other Anansi tales offer explanations as to why crows are bald (tale 47, “Why John-crow Has a Bald Head”), why dogs watch people while they eat (tale 48, “Why Dog is Always Looking”), and why river rocks have moss (tale 49, “Why Rocks at the River are Covered with Moss”). Other tales in Beckwith’s collection that explain habits and characteristics of other animals do not feature Anansi at all. For example, Anansi does not appear in tale 51, “Why Hog is Always Grunting,” or in tale 52, “Why Toad Croaks.”

Some of the tales have also been told in other slaveholding regions. The story of Anansi and the Tar-baby (tales 21 and 59), for example, may be familiar to American readers who remember the Uncle Remus stories, which were collected by [Joel Chandler Harris](https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/history/joel-chandler-harris) in the late nineteenth century and were popularized by Walt Disney in the 1946 film _Song of the South_. In Beckwith’s collection, tale 21 includes three variants, one of which claims to explain that Anansi lives under the rafters due to his shame at being caught by the Tar-baby.

Although Anansi is known as a trickster, he does not always prove to be clever. In “The Yam-hills,” tale 31, Monkey tricks Anansi, which results in Anansi’s death. It is forbidden to speak the word “nine” (which is the number of yam hills Anansi has planted), and whoever says the number aloud dies. Anansi tricks both Hog and Goat into counting all the hills. Each counts to nine and dies, and Anansi takes each animal home to eat. Monkey observes this from a tree and when asked to count the yam hills, he angers Anansi by counting one through eight and concluding with “an’ the one Br’er \[Brother\] Anansi sit down upon.” After he repeats this, Anansi grows impatient, tries to correct him, says the word “nine,” and instantly dies.

The final sections of Beckwith’s collections deal less directly with Anansi. Tales 50 through 62 do not directly concern Anansi, although they are stories of animals. In the section “Old Stories, Chiefly of Sorcery” (tales 63–99), a few of the tales feature Anansi. Tale 100, “Ali Baba and Kissem” begins the modern European stories, some of which do include Anansi tales. For example, in tale 130, “Clever Molly May,” someone else outwits Anansi; his servant eats the turkey she has roasted and blames the guest, after warning him that Anansi is sharpening his knives to cut off the guest’s hands. Some of the songs recorded in “Song and Dance” (which are sometimes given with musical notation) include Anansi as well.

Bibliography
------------

Barry, Peter. Beginning Theory. 3rd ed. Manchester: Manchester UP, 2009. Print.

Beckwith, Martha Warren. Jamaica Anansi Stories. 1924. Charleston: BiblioBazaar, 2007. Print.

Brooker, Peter. A Glossary of Cultural Theory. 2nd ed. London: Arnold, 2002. Print.

Marshall, Emily Zobel. Anansi’s Journey: A Story of Jamaican Cultural Resistance. Kingston: U of West Indies P, 2012. Print.

Pelton, Robert D. TheTrickster in West Africa: A Study of Mythic Irony and Sacred Delight. Berkeley: U of California P, 1980. Print.

\---. “West African Tricksters: Web of Purpose, Dance of Delight.” Mythical Trickster Figures: Contours, Contexts, and Criticisms. Ed. William J. Hynes and William G. Doty. Tuscaloosa: U of Alabama P, 1993, 122–40. Print.

Van Duin, Lieke. “Anansi as Classical Hero.” Journal of Caribbean Literatures 5.1 (2007): 33–42. Print.

Vecsey, Christopher. “The Exception Who Proves the Rules.” Mythical Trickster Figures: Contours, Contexts, and Criticisms. Ed. William J. Hynes and William G. Doty. Tuscaloosa: U of Alabama P, 1993. 106–21. Print.

Click here for more information.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/94/Symbol_support_vote.svg/20px-Symbol_support_vote.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Good_articles* "This is a good article. Click here for more information.") From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
The Doctor
The Fugitive Doctor
Doctor Who character

Jo Martin as the Fugitive Doctor

First appearance"Fugitive of the Judoon" (2020)
Last appearance"The Story & the Engine" (2025)
Introduced byChris Chibnall
Portrayed byJo Martin
Information
Appearances5 stories (5 episodes)
Companions
  • Lee Clayton[1][2][3]
  • Karvanista[4]
Chronology
  • Series 12 (2020)
  • Series 13 (2021)
  • Specials (2022)
  • Series 15 (2025)
The **Fugitive Doctor**[\[a\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-FugitiveName-5) is an incarnation of [the Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Doctor_/(Doctor_Who/) "The Doctor (Doctor Who)"), the protagonist of the British [science fiction television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_fiction_on_television "Science fiction on television") series _[Doctor Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who "Doctor Who")_. She is portrayed by [Jo Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin "Jo Martin"), the first black actor to play the Doctor. The character first appeared in the [twelfth series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_12 "Doctor Who series 12") of the programme's revival in "[Fugitive of the Judoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_of_the_Judoon "Fugitive of the Judoon")" (2020), where she was disguised as a woman named Ruth Clayton in 21st century [Gloucester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gloucester "Gloucester"). Eventually, she restores her memories, and it is revealed that Ruth is an incarnation of the Doctor, though her placement in the chronology of the series is initially unclear. Within the programme's narrative, the Doctor is a Time Lord, from the planet [Gallifrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallifrey "Gallifrey"). The Doctor travels in a [time-travelling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_travel "Time travel") [space ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spacecraft "Spacecraft"), the [TARDIS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TARDIS "TARDIS"). Possessing alien [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology "Physiology"), the Doctor, when critically injured, can [regenerate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regeneration_/(Doctor_Who/) "Regeneration (Doctor Who)") into a new body, gaining a new physical appearance and personality. This [plot device](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plot_device "Plot device") has allowed a number of actors, both male and female, to portray the Doctor through the decades. Each actor to play the Doctor offers a different take on the Doctor's essential personality. A [fugitive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive "Fugitive"), this incarnation of the Doctor is considered to be a more ruthless incarnation, and formerly worked for [Time Lord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Lord "Time Lord") [black ops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_ops "Black ops") group "The Division", from whom she is now on the run. This incarnation was conceived by showrunner [Chris Chibnall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Chibnall "Chris Chibnall") and co-writer [Vinay Patel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinay_Patel "Vinay Patel"), with the pair coming up with the incarnation late into writing the script of "Fugitive of the Judoon". The Fugitive Doctor was included not only to foreshadow the upcoming "Timeless Child" arc of series 12, but also to act as a surprise twist within "Fugitive of the Judoon". The incarnation would go on to reappear multiple times within the show following her debut. The Fugitive Doctor received a mostly positive reception from critics, who praised the casting of a black woman as the Doctor and highlighted the performance of Martin. Many fans and critics expressed interest in seeing Martin reprise the role in a larger capacity. Some critics criticised the usage and execution of the character's concept within the series. Martin has expressed interest in continuing to portray the role, and has appeared in several [Big Finish Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Finish_Productions "Big Finish Productions") [audio dramas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_dramas "Audio dramas") depicting stories starring the Fugitive Doctor. She has also stated that the role had helped her expand her career prospects, particularly in America. The Fugitive Doctor first appears in the 2020 episode "[Fugitive of the Judoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_of_the_Judoon "Fugitive of the Judoon")", disguised as human tour guide Ruth Clayton by means of a [Chameleon Arch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Nature_/(Doctor_Who/) "Human Nature (Doctor Who)"). As Ruth, she lives alongside her "husband" Lee in 21st century [Gloucester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gloucester "Gloucester") with Ruth having no knowledge of her true nature. Intergalactic alien police force the [Judoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judoon "Judoon") locate her and invade the city, intending to present her to [Galifreyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallifreyan "Gallifreyan") Commander Gat, who plans to return the Doctor to Gallifreyan [black ops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_ops "Black ops") group the Division after the Doctor fled from them.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-decider-6) Lee, [companion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Companion_/(Doctor_Who/) "Companion (Doctor Who)") to the Fugitive Doctor and a fellow Time Lord, directs Ruth to a lighthouse, where her memories are restored.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Bacon-7) At the same time, the [Thirteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteenth_Doctor "Thirteenth Doctor") finds a police box buried in the grounds – Ruth's [TARDIS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TARDIS "TARDIS"). As they reveal their identities to one another, it transpires that neither Doctor recognises the other, leading to confusion between the pair as they both assumed the other was a future version of herself. After tricking Gat into accidentally killing herself with a malfunctioning gun, the Fugitive Doctor parts with the Thirteenth Doctor acrimoniously.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Telegraph-8) She reappears briefly in "[The Timeless Children](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Timeless_Children "The Timeless Children")", when the Thirteenth Doctor is trapped in the Time Lord storage database the [Matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matrix_/(Doctor_Who/) "Matrix (Doctor Who)") by the [Master](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Master_/(Doctor_Who/) "The Master (Doctor Who)"). He informs her that she is the Timeless Child, and had lived many lives prior to what she believed to be her [first incarnation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Doctor "First Doctor"). In trying to escape and reconcile this knowledge with her identity, she encounters a projection of the Fugitive Doctor. The projection reminds her that she has never previously been defined by her past before disappearing.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Mulkern-9) The Fugitive Doctor reappears in "[Once, Upon Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Once,_Upon_Time "Once, Upon Time")".[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Fullerton-10) In that episode, the Thirteenth Doctor experiences flashbacks to a raid by the Fugitive Doctor on a location known as the Temple of Atropos, where the Fugitive Doctor confronted the Ravagers known as [Swarm and Azure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swarm_and_Azure "Swarm and Azure"). The Thirteenth Doctor learns that the Fugitive Doctor had led a team of Division operatives, including the Lupari officer [Karvanista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karvanista "Karvanista"), to capture the two Ravagers and uses her past self's methods as an inspiration to resolve a situation involving the Ravagers in the future.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-11) The Fugitive Doctor reappears in "[The Power of the Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Power_of_the_Doctor "The Power of the Doctor")" as an [AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI "AI") hologram which is used to trick the Master after he has stolen the Doctor's body.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-12) The Fugitive Doctor is later seen as a memory from a past adventure involving [Anansi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anansi "Anansi") and his daughter Abena in the [Fifteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifteenth_Doctor "Fifteenth Doctor") story, "[The Story & the Engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Story_%26_the_Engine "The Story & the Engine")".[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Griffin-2025-13) ### Spin-off appearances \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fugitive_Doctor&action=edit§ion=2 "Edit section: Spin-off appearances")\] On 23 April 2022, [Big Finish Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Finish_Productions "Big Finish Productions") announced that Jo Martin would reprise her role for _[The Fugitive Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Doctor_Who:_The_New_Series_audio_plays_by_Big_Finish#The_Fugitive_Doctor_Adventures_\(2025%E2%80%93present\) "List of Doctor Who: The New Series audio plays by Big Finish")_, a series of _Doctor Who_ audio dramas following her incarnation of the Doctor after the events of "[Fugitive of the Judoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_of_the_Judoon "Fugitive of the Judoon")".[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-14) Martin would later appear in the _Once and Future_ series of _Doctor Who_ audio dramas.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-15) Producer David Richardson wanted to have audio drama stories depicting the Fugitive Doctor, and discussed with Chibnall about the character's backstory to avoid conflicting with Chibnall's established history for the character. To avoid conflicts between ongoing Big Finish series and the character's backstory, Richardson and his team elected to focus the Fugitive Doctor's audio drama adventures following her time with the Division, and to avoid answering any major questions about who her character is.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Tantimedh-2024-16) The character starred in a series of comic strips produced by [Titan Publishing Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titan_Publishing_Group "Titan Publishing Group"), which depicted how the incarnation became a fugitive.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-17) An action figure depicting the Fugitive Doctor was released in 2024.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-18) In July 2025, BBC Studios announced that the Fugitive Doctor will feature in a new mixed-media event called _Circuit Breaker_ with Jo Martin reprising her role as the Fugitive Doctor. Author Esmie Jikiemi-Pearson has been confirmed as overseeing the narrative arc, which will span audio dramas, comics, mobile games, novels and other forms of "digital storytelling".[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-19) Conception and development -------------------------- \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fugitive_Doctor&action=edit§ion=6 "Edit section: Conception and development")\] ### Creation and naming \[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fugitive_Doctor&action=edit§ion=7 "Edit section: Creation and naming")\] [![Image 3](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/89/Chris_Chibnall_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg/250px-Chris_Chibnall_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chris_Chibnall_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg) The Fugitive Doctor was conceived by writer and then- showrunner [Chris Chibnall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Chibnall "Chris Chibnall") (pictured) alongside the co-writer of "Fugitive of the Judoon", [Vinay Patel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinay_Patel "Vinay Patel"). The inclusion of the Fugitive Doctor was developed late into the writing process of "[Fugitive of the Judoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_of_the_Judoon "Fugitive of the Judoon")", with the script lining up to make her inclusion make sense within the episode. Then-showrunner [Chris Chibnall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Chibnall "Chris Chibnall") and co-writer [Vinay Patel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinay_Patel "Vinay Patel") developed the idea of the incarnation together, and sought to keep it as much of a secret as possible; the return and on-location shoots of the [Judoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judoon "Judoon") were used to distract fans from the presence of the Fugitive Doctor, which website _[Gizmodo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gizmodo "Gizmodo")_ framed as "making sure everybody was too distracted to try and piece it together for themselves."[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-20) The character had no distinct name separate from other incarnations of the Doctor, leading to fans giving her various nicknames, such as the "Ruthless Doctor", a play on the character Ruth's name. The name "Fugitive Doctor", named by fans after her debut episode, eventually stuck as the name of the character, with it being used in an official capacity from the episode "[Once, Upon Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Once,_Upon_Time "Once, Upon Time")" onwards.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-21) Fans also initially theorized that the character was an incarnation from a parallel universe, but Chibnall disconfirmed this, stating that she was "definitively" an incarnation of the Doctor.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-22) Though the incarnation does not lead an entire series of her own, Whittaker stated that the Fugitive incarnation was treated like "like any actor taking on the role permanently".[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-23) Further appearances of the character were not initially planned for [_Doctor Who_ series 13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_13 "Doctor Who series 13"), according to Chibnall, but he said that he would consider it due to how widely popular and accepted the Fugitive Doctor had become within the _Doctor Who_ fanbase.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-24) The character would eventually appear in an episode of the series.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Fullerton-10) The character's further cameo re-appearance in [series 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_series_15 "Doctor Who series 15") episode "[The Story & the Engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Story_%26_the_Engine "The Story & the Engine")" was done as a result of the episode's focus on the Doctor's ethnicity. Showrunner [Russell T Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell_T_Davies "Russell T Davies") stated that "it felt like Jo Martin was missing", and that he wanted to "acknowledge her" in the episode to show that the character "still exists".[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Episode_BTS-25) [![Image 4](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9b/Jo_Martin.jpg/250px-Jo_Martin.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jo_Martin.jpg) [Jo Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin "Jo Martin") (pictured) portrays the Fugitive Doctor in the character's appearances on-screen. The Fugitive Doctor is portrayed by actress [Jo Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Martin "Jo Martin"). It was not announced prior to the broadcast of the character's first appearance in "Fugitive of the Judoon" that a new Doctor would be debuting. Promotional materials credited Jo Martin only as playing Ruth, while the actress herself was not told that she would be playing the Doctor until she was offered the part after her audition. She was then only able to tell her husband about the character's true identity.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Ruthless-26) Martin had been a fan of the series, having grown up watching [Colin Baker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_Baker "Colin Baker")'s [portrayal of the character](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sixth_Doctor "Sixth Doctor").[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Mensah-2024-27) Martin's incarnation is the series' first on-screen black Doctor,[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Bundel-2020-28) and additionally the first on-screen black and female Doctor.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Fullerton-2021-29) She is the second woman to portray the Doctor, following [Jodie Whittaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jodie_Whittaker "Jodie Whittaker")'s [Thirteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteenth_Doctor "Thirteenth Doctor").[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Salem-2022-30) As a middle-aged black woman, Martin initially believed that her portraying the Doctor would be incredibly unlikely. She was happy with her casting as she believed it "set the standard" for the series going forward.[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Fullerton-2021-29) Martin revealed that she was happy the character was able to act as a black role model for young viewers of the series.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-31) Following her appearances on-screen, Martin stated she was interested in potentially doing a spin-off following her incarnation of the Doctor,[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Fullerton-2021-29) and has expressed interest in returning to the series.[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Griffin-2025-13) Martin stated that she "would love to do more audios" alongside potential television appearances. She also stated that she hopes that the Fugitive Doctor's past will be explored more.[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Hibbs-2025-32) The Fugitive Doctor is a "darker" incarnation of the character, with an "acerbic tongue" and a short temper. She is a battle-hardened figure who does not [suffer fools gladly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suffer_fools_gladly "Suffer fools gladly"), with an authoritative and composed demeanour who will happily use weapons if necessary.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Ruthless-26) Unlike all other incarnations of the character, Martin's Doctor will readily make use of available weaponry to decisively end conflict. She exhibited this violent streak when she attacked a [Judoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judoon "Judoon"), before manipulating a foe into unknowingly killing themselves with it.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Telegraph-8) Her Big Finish characterization depicts her as having a similar moral compass to other incarnations of the character, however, with her audio drama stories depicting a conflict between her fugitive nature and her desire to help others.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Tantimedh-2024-16) Aspects of her character were inspired by [Peter Capaldi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Capaldi "Peter Capaldi")'s [Twelfth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twelfth_Doctor "Twelfth Doctor"), with Martin stating that the Fugitive Doctor has "got an edge and a dark side to her as well as being cheeky and charming. And she doesn't really have a filter."[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Fullerton-2020-33) The character is intended to reference earlier incarnations of the Doctor in order to suggest that she is from the [Thirteenth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteenth_Doctor "Thirteenth Doctor")'s past. She declines to use a [sonic screwdriver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonic_screwdriver "Sonic screwdriver") and refers to the [TARDIS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TARDIS "TARDIS") as her "ship", much like the [First Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Doctor "First Doctor").[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Bacon-7) Chibnall revealed that he intentionally did not wish to confirm where Martin's incarnation was in the timeline,[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-34) though an infographic published in the official _[Doctor Who Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_Magazine "Doctor Who Magazine")_ explicitly places her before the [First Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Doctor "First Doctor") but prior to the Doctors seen in _[The Brain of Morbius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brain_of_Morbius "The Brain of Morbius")_.[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-35) The interior of her TARDIS is also modelled after the set used in the 1960s, with white walls and an identical central console.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Ruthless-26)[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-36) The character's costume was designed by Ray Holman to reflect her sterner nature. Black [combat trousers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cargo_pants "Cargo pants") and boots reference the costume of the Twelfth Doctor, and additionally are meant to indicate the character has experienced combat. She also wears a dark-coloured Scottish [tweed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tweed "Tweed") [waistcoat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waistcoat "Waistcoat") and [frock coat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frock_coat "Frock coat"), with the tweed being included to reference [Matt Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Smith "Matt Smith")'s [Eleventh Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eleventh_Doctor "Eleventh Doctor"), who was the first Doctor Holman designed for. The coat is period cut in reference to several "Classic series" (1963–89) Doctors.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Fullerton-2020-33)[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Ray-37) A brightly coloured [shirt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shirt "Shirt") with a stand collar and frilled cuffs are used for their contrasting styles, used to represent the character's eccentric personality traits[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Ian-38) and were made from African [Kente cloth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kente_cloth "Kente cloth") as a tribute to the actor's heritage and the significance of her casting. This Doctor has also occasionally worn a pair of yellow sunglasses with this outfit.[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Ray-37) Jo Martin was cast as the programme's first black Doctor, a milestone which was met with much praise from commentators.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Bundel-2020-28) Martin stated that she had received many messages from fans across the world who thanked her for portraying the role.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Mensah-2024-27) Martin explained in an interview with _[Radio Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Times "Radio Times")_ that the series had put her "on the map" in America, which "upgraded the kind of jobs" Martin was able to get.[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Hibbs-2025-32) Martin's performance was lauded by critics,[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Patrick-2)[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-39) and several critics and fans have expressed a desire to see the character return on-screen in larger capacities.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Mulkern-9)[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-40)[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-41)[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-42) The character's introduction resulted in large amount of [fan art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fan_art "Fan art"), as well as [fan theories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fan_theories "Fan theories") about her potential origins and place in the Doctor's wider timeline.[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-43) Adi Tantimedh from _[Bleeding Cool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bleeding_Cool "Bleeding Cool")_ wrote that the Fugitive Doctor had "proven surprisingly popular among fans", which Tantimedh cited as being a result of her "no-nonsense stillness". Olivia Garret from _Radio Times_ praised Martin's performance as the Doctor, similarly writing that Martin's incarnation "encapsulated everything the Doctor should be", highlighting the Fugitive Doctor's harsh yet gentle character.[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-44) Morgan Jeffrey, in another article for _Radio Times_, believed that the Fugitive Doctor's introduction broke the series' history of frequently sidelining or killing off notable black supporting characters, and that the character, who was portrayed by a middle-aged black woman, allowed many people to see themselves in the Doctor that many previous actors had not been able to depict before.[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-45) Merryana Salem of _[Junkee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junkee "Junkee")_ criticised the direction of Martin's incarnation, believing that making the only explicit "criminal" of the Doctor's incarnations black invoked harmful stereotypes, while also opining that the introduction of an earlier female Doctor prior to Whittaker undermined Whittaker's own importance within the larger context of the series.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-Salem-2022-30) Tantimedh, in another article for _Bleeding Cool_, felt Chibnall failed to capitalise on the Fugitive Doctor, with Tantimedh feeling as though the character was introduced purely for shock value rather than for any tangible expansion within the show itself. Though Tantimedh hoped to see more of the incarnation, she believed that Chibnall "robbed Jo Martin and the show of the fanfare of the first woman of colour to play The Doctor."[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_note-46) 1. **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive_Doctor#cite_ref-FugitiveName_5-0)** In her first two appearances, the character is credited only as "the Doctor" and is only ever referred to as such within the show.
